Sir Edward Knatchbull, Bart., who represented East Kent for several years, by his second wife, Fanny Catherine, daughter of Edward Knight, Esq., of Godmersham Park, and Chawton House, Hants. Born at Mersham Hatch, 1829; married, 1852, Anna Maria Elizabeth, youngest daughter of the Rev. Mares R. Southwell. Educated at Eton and at Magdalen College, Oxford, where he graduated 1850. Assumed the name of Hugessen in addition to his patronymic. Is a magistrate and deputy-lieutenant of Kent, and member of parliament for Sandwich, Deal, and Walmer; was a lord of the treasury from June, 1859, till May, 1866; appointed under secretary of state for the home department, May, 1866; resigned July in same year, and reappointed Dec., 1868; and under-secretary of state for the colonies, Jan. 1871, to Feb. 20, 1874. Author of 'Stories for my Children,' 'Crackers for Christmas,' 'Moonshine,' &c., &c.

HUGGINS, HASTINGS, C., LL.D.—Stipendiary magistrate at British Guiana; called to bar, Inner Temple, Jan. 1858; was Queen's counsel, solicitor-general, and speaker of the house of assembly, and member of the executive council at Nevis; and in 1861 completed a revised compilation of the laws of that island, from 1681 to 1861 inclusive; appointed in 1861 attorney-general of British Honduras, and became ex officio member of the executive council of that colony.

HUGGINS, HORATIO JAMES.—Queen's advocate of Sierra Leone from 9th May, 1863, and chairman of commissioners "for the settlement of claims to land," from 1st Sept. 1863. Is member of the executive and legislative councils; has acted as chief justice on three occasions; became judge ad interim of the mixed courts of justice under the slave trade treaties, on the death of Mr. Skelton, on 21st May, 1865, until the 19th March, 1866; was sent as chief commissioner, with Major Ireland, of the 3rd West India regiment, to the Moriah country, in June, 1865, to effect the release of British subjects seized and imprisoned during the war then raging in that territory between King Boharry and his nephew, Malaghi Bally, and to prevent further injury to life and property; and again as sole commissioner on a second commission to the same country in July, 1865, receiving on both occasions the thanks of the government for the readiness with which he undertook the duties and the "ability he displayed." He also acted as attorney-general in the island of St. Vincent in 1857 and 1858. He was educated at a military college in France, and called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn in Hilary Term, 1838; chief justice, Sierra Leone, 1876.

HULL, HENRY JOCELYN.—Clerk in civil service, Tasmania, August, 1847; finance clerk in lands and works department, February, 1852; deputy commissioner of crown lands, 1st July, 1873.

HULL, HUGH MUNRO.—Clerk to the governor of Tasmania, April, 1834; senior clerk, colonial secretary's office, July, 1841; statistician and secretary to committee of officers, 1844; police magistrate, J.P., coroner, and chairman of quarter sessions, 1866; clerk assistant in parliament, 1857; captain 2nd Volunteer Rifles, 1860; clerk of the house of assembly, April, 1864; was secretary to the reception committee of H.R.H. the Duke of Edinburgh, and also to inter-colonial exhibition commission, and secretary to the Philadelphia exhibition commission; author of "Forty years in Tasmania," "Tasmania in 1871," "Hints to Emigrants," and "Tasmania as a field for British Emigration;" is a fellow of the royal colonial institute and corresponding secretary for Tasmania.
HULL, HUGH.—Librarian to the parliamentary library, Tasmania, April, 1867.

HULL, W. WINSTANLEY.—Appointed clerk in the office of the governor-in-chief of the Windward Islands, Barbados, November, 1872; promoted chief clerk, August, 1873.

HUME, W. W.—Appointed acting assistant to the government agent for the western province, Ceylon, 1848; deputy fiscal, and acting assistant agent for the central province, Oct. 1849, 1853; commissioner of requests, Jaffna, in that colony, 1854; temple land commissioner, 1859; senior temple land commissioner, 1860; assistant government agent and commissioner of requests, Mattle, 1865; fiscal, western province, 1867; acting government agent, eastern province, Nov. 1872; appointment confirmed, June, 1873.

HUMPHREYS, WM.—From 20th Aug., 1835, to March, 1837, in H.M.'s customs at Dominica, when he was appointed secretary to the commissioners of compensation; July, 1837, to June, 1838, private secretary to Governor Light, of Dominica; July, 1838, to Jan. 1841, private secretary to Governor Light, British Guiana, and also assistant government secretary; 1843, stipendiary magistrate, and immigration agent general; March, 1853, stipendiary magistrate; sheriff of Essequebo, March, 1863.

HUNT, CAPTAIN JOHN CALVIN.—Half-pay; joined Austrian army, 1844; served in 5th cuirassier regiment; served at siege of Vienna, 1848, and campaign in Hungary; was present at all actions during the campaign; captain, 1852; was with the army of observation on the Vistula and Bukovina, in Poland, 1854; received extra certificates and thanks from the Emperor of Austria for good service and bravery; in 1855 proceeded to England, and joined the cavalry of the British German Legion; in Nov. 1856, proceeded with German Legion to the Cape of Good Hope, where he was employed until disbanded, in 1860; appointed acting deputy-assistant commissary-general at East London, British Kaffraria, 1860; Sept. 1861, appointed acting special magistrate to the Ganobie district, British Kaffraria; Feb. 1870, appointed civil commissioner and resident magistrate of Paddie.

HUNT, R. F.—Was appointed clerk to the colonial secretary of Bermuda, Sept. 10th, 1875.

HUNTER, A.—Public medical officer, British Honduras.

HUXTABLE, HENRY ANTHONY.—Has been in the office of the procureur-general of Mauritius since the 1st of February, 1868; appointed in June, 1872, a clerk to the royal commissioners of inquiry into the treatment of immigrants in Mauritius.

HYDE, CHARLES TUNSTALL—Was private secretary and aide-de-camp to Governor Hill at Antigua in 1863 was appointed inspector-general of police in that island, March, 1867, and auditor-general of the colony in May, 1867; administered the government of the Virgin Islands from July to end of Oct. 1869; appointed provost-marshal of Barbados, 1870.

IBBOTT, JOHN THOMAS.—Sub-controller of customs and sub-bookkeeper, Berbice, 16th March, 1875; acting tide waiter, Georgetown, Demerara, from the 9th July, 1869, to the 1st of Feb., 1860; clerk in charge of the colonial bonded warehouse, Georgetown, 1st Feb., 1860; acting sub-controller of customs and sub-bookkeeper, Berbice, from the 9th Sept., 1869, to the 23rd December, 1870; acting assistant government secretary, and acting receiver-general, Berbice, from the 24th Dec., 1870, to the 23rd March, 1872; appointed on the 16th Feb., 1870, 1st clerk to the customs, Georgetown, Demerara; assumed the duties on the 23rd March, 1872; acted as comptroller of customs in 1872, 1874, and 1876.

IMLACH, ROBERT WIGHT.—Crown solicitor, British Guiana.

INGLOTT, FERDINANDO V., C.M.G.—Was appointed a teacher of a government primary school at Malta, Nov. 1841; served in the naval department from 1843 to 1855; assistant superintendent of ports, 1858; comptroller of charitable institutions, Jan. 1859; is ex officio member of council.

INNES, SIR JOSEPH GEORGE LONG, KNIGHT BACHELOR (creat. 1875).—Eldest son of Captain Joseph Long Innes, late H.M. 89th regiment of foot. Born at Sydney, N.S.W., October 16th, 1834. Educated at the King's School, Paramatta. Called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn, Michaelmas term, 1859 (certificate of honour, Trinity term, 1859). Admitted to bar of New South Wales, February, 1862. Appointed district judge in Queensland, December, 1865; resigned that office and returned to practice at bar of N. S. W., July, 1869; elected member of legislative assembly, March, 1872; solicitor-general of N. S. W., 14th May, 1872; attorney-general 20th November, 1873, to 9th February, 1875. In Aug., 1872, was called to the upper house of parliament in N. S. W., in which chamber he represented the government. In Sept.-Oct., 1874, accompanied Sir Hercules Robinson on his special mission in connection with the annexation of Fiji. For his services on that occasion received the honour of knighthood.

INNES, J. R.—Civil commissioner and resident magistrate of Bedford division, Cape of Good Hope; appointed Oct. 1867; also inspector of roads; was teacher in government schools, 1842; clerk to superintendent-general of education, 1845; clerk in colonial secretary's office, 1847 to 1856; magistrate of Riversdale, 1856-1868; ditto of Urtenhage, 1863 to 1857.

INNISS, WILLIAM E.—Joined the civil service at Sierra Leone in the surveyor's department, December, 1866, as artizan till June, 1871; held the appointment of under goaler, June, 1871, to December, 1872, then transferred to the harbour works as artificer; appointed keeper of the gaol, August, 1874.

IRVING, CHARLES J.—Was in the colonial land and emigration office from June 1852 to Nov. 1853; clerk in the audit office, Somerset House, from Nov. 1853 to July 1864, when he was appointed special clerk, audit office, Mauritius; appointed auditor-general of the Straits Settlements and member of the executive and legislative councils of the colony, 1st April, 1867.

IRVING, EDWARD.—Was in the colonial land and emigration office from April, 1852, until 1st January, 1855, when he was appointed private secretary to Sir F. Sandford, December, 1868; assistant colonial secretary, Straits Settlements, 20th November, 1869; acting auditor-general, January to July, 1870, and again from March, 1874, to the end of the year.

IRVING, HENRY T., C.M.G. (1874).—Appointed clerk in colonial office, November, 1854; promoted to 3rd class, October, 1859; appointed private secretary to Sir F. Rogers, now Lord Blachford, under-secretary of state, 1862; promoted to 2nd class, April, 1863; appointed colonial secretary of

ISEMONGER, EDWIN EMPSON.—Appointed to the audit office, London, 7th February, 1856; chief clerk to auditor-general, Straits Settlements, 4th Sept. 1867; was acting colonial treasurer, commissioner of stamps, accountant-general to the supreme court, and member of both councils, Straits Settlements, from 3rd March, 1869, to 10th May, 1870; appointed assistant treasurer, Straits Settlements, Nov. 1869; is justice of the peace for the Settlements; placed in charge of Malacca treasury and stamp offices, September, 1872; duties of collector of land revenue added, February, 1874; appointed magistrate of police and commissioner of court of requests, Malacca, 1st June, 1874.

JACKSON, CHARLES HAMILTON.—Appointed island secretary for Jamaica, and official member of the legislative council, 1878; island secretary and administrator general.

JACKSON, FRANCIS EDWARD.—M.B., University of Aberdeen; member of the royal college of surgeons of England; member and licentiate of the apothecaries' society of London; certificated by the Privy Council as a public vaccinator; studied at Saint Bartholomew's Hospital, the London Hospital, and University of Aberdeen; colonial surgeon, province Wellesley, Penang, 1874; magistrate and J.P. for the Settlement of Penang; superintendent of vaccination for province Wellesley.

JACKSON, MAXIMILIAN JAMES.—Special magistrate and inspector under Northern Border Protection Act, appointed October, 1868, Cape of Good Hope; was clerk at Victoria (East), 1858 to 1864; ditto at Richmond, 1864 to 1865; acting C. C. and R. M. Richmond, for four months during this period; clerk at Murraysburg, 1865 to 1868; C. C. and R. M. Richmond, 1873.

JACKSON, HARRY M., Lieut., R.N.—Appointed A.D.C. to governor of Trinidad, Sept., 1874; private secretary, Nov., 1874.

JACKSON, THOMAS W.—Appointed magistrate at the Gambia, 1869; a puisne judge, Gold Coast, 1876.

JACOBS, SIMON.—Is attorney-general, Cape of Good Hope, appointed, 1874; obtained a licence from the Hon. Society of the Inner Temple to practise as a special pleader, November, 1861; called to the bar, 17th Nov., 1852; admitted as an advocate of the supreme court, Cape of Good Hope, Dec., 1860; appointed attorney-general of British Kaffraria, 4th April, 1861; solicitor-general, Cape of Good Hope, 1866.

JAMES, JOHN CHARLES HORSEY.—Born at Rome, 1841; educated at Rugby and at Exeter College, Oxford, where he graduated B.A., 1864; called to the bar by the Inner Temple, Nov., 1866, and is a member of the Oxford circuit; appointed commissioner of titles in Western Australia, July 9th, 1875.

JANISCH, H. R.—Appointed police magistrate, St. Helena, from 1851; was acting queen's advocate 1856, 1857; and acting colonial secretary, 1861 and 1868; has been in colonial service since 1888; was colonial secretary and auditor-general; Governor of St. Helena, 1873.

JAUNCEY, FRANCIS HASTINGS.—Appointed 5th Nov., 1871; cashier in Treasury, Lagos, 1st January, 1872, private secretary to Sir John Hawley Glover, G.C.M.G., and clerk of council same colony, 15th July, 1875; appointed Registrar of Titles, Western Australia, under the Transfer Land Act, 1874.

JEANS, JOSEPH HENRY.—Formerly colonial surgeon, Bathurst, Gambia, appointed Oct., 1867; licentiate royal college of physicians; member royal college of surgeons; licentiate apothecaries' company; staff assistant surgeon, Canterbury; surgeon to H.M.S. Adriatic; hon. surgeon to 2nd Hampshire Light Horse; coroner; officer of health; quarantine officer of health; magistrate; commissioner of the court of requests for the above settlement. Commoner, Downing College, Cambridge; and Pensioner at Christ's College; now assistant surgeon at Lagos.

JERKILL, HERBERT.—Received commission as lieutenant in royal engineers, 17th April, 1866; employed under War Office and Trinity House in submarine mining and destruction of sunken ships, from 1868 to 1870, and under G.P.O. in the telegraph department, from 1870 to 1873, and 1874 to 1876; served in the campaign of 1873-74 on the Gold Coast under Sir Garnet Wolseley; appointed private secretary to the Earl of Carnarvon, January, 1877.

JENKINS, J. W.—Colonial surveyor, superintendent of public works, commissioner of roads, &c., Sierra Leone, May, 1868.

JENNINGS, MATTHEW.—Sub-collector of customs, Port Elizabeth, appointed 1st July, 1870; appointed clerk in the customs departments, Cape Town, Sept., 1848; acting sub-collector at Port Beaufort, 1850; sub-collector, East London, 1851; controller of customs and navigation laws, 1852; shipping-master and justice of the peace for the port of East London, 1855; resident magistrate of the district of East London, 1857; immigration agent, 1858; collector of customs for British Kaffraria, 1859; civil commissioner, East London, Cape of Good Hope.

JERVOIS, COLONEL SIR WILLIAM FRANCIS DRUMMOND, K.C.M.G. (1874), C.B., R.E.—Served at the Cape of Good Hope from April, 1841, until September, 1848, of which time he was six years on the frontier and in Kaffraria. In 1842 he was appointed to the staff as brigade-major to a force of all arms sent on an expedition against the Dutch Boers; served during the Kaffir war of 1846-7, accompanying Sir Henry Pottinger and Lieutenant-general Sir George Berkeley to the scene of hostilities; was engaged during the war in active operations generally, and in making a military map of Kaffraria, which was subsequently engraved and published; in 1845-6 visited Natal, and returning overland to the Cape Colony, he laid down a map of the country between the two colonies. During the six years he served on the frontier, he was also engaged in making surveys, in constructing roads, building bridges, and improving the communications of the country. From 1852 to 1855 was specially employed at Alderney in designing and executing the fortifications of that island. From 1856 to 1875 was on the staff of the war office, first as assistant inspector-general of fortifications, and subsequently as deputy-director of fortifications. From 1857 to 1875 was secretary of the committee on the defence of the empire, and in 1859 he was secretary to the royal commission on national defences. During the time he was in the war office he was employed in the design and execution of, and on the business connected with the whole of the extensive works of fortifications now nearly completed in this country, and in the British foreign possessions; in 1863 was nominated
a civil C.B.; in 1863 was sent to Canada, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Bermuda, to report on the defences of those provinces; and again in 1864 to confer with the Canadian government as to the defences of the dominion. His proposals were approved by the imperial and colonial authorities, and those for Bermuda and Quebec have been adopted and carried out; in 1865 was sent to Malta, and in 1866 to Gibraltar, to prepare projects for the improvement of the defences at those fortresses. He again visited Halifax and Bermuda in 1869, and made further reports on the defences; in 1871-2 was employed by the government of India to inspect and report upon the defences of Aden, Perim, Bombay, and the Hooghly; and submitted reports to the secretary of state for India in council respecting the defences of those places. By desire of the viceroy of India, and with the approval of the secretary of state for India, he also visited British Burmah, and subsequently submitted reports with regard to the defences of Rangoon and Moulmein. Appointed to the order of St. Michael and St. George for his colonial services; in April, 1875, appointed governor of the Straits Settlements.

JEVERS, R. W.—Educated at the Queen's University in Ireland, where he graduated in classics with honours; appointed writer in the Ceylon civil service, April, 1872.

JEWELL, R. R.—Clerk of the works in Western Australia; appointed 1853.

JOHNSON, SAMUEL OTIS.—Member of the Executive Council, Bahamas, 1875.

JOHNSON, THOMAS.—Appointed clerk to the government steamer 'Gambia,' 1847; third writer in the colonial secretary's office, Gambia, 1852; colonial registrar, 1855; registrar of deeds, 7th June, 1858, lieutenant of the British Combo militia, 12th April, 1862; served as second writer, 1852; and as postmaster, 1859 and 1860, and again in 1869; promoted second writer, and collector of rates for local improvements, Dec., 1862; acting as colonial engineer from Aug., 1866, to Dec., 1868; promoted to the office of first clerk and cashier in the collector and treasurer's office, Jan. 1, 1869.

JOHNSON, D. S.—Appointed dispenser in hospital at Sierra Leone, 17th Dec., 1858; promoted sanitary inspector, February, 1857.

JOHNSTON, W. W. W.—Lieutenant-colonel; entered the army, 1854; as a subaltern frequently employed on the staff in the West Indies and on the West Coast of Africa; promoted captain, 1862; commanded the troops in Honduras in 1864; aide-de-camp to major-general O'Connor, C.B., commanding the forces in Jamaica, &c., 1865; at the outbreak of the Jamaica disturbances same year, appointed deputy adjutant-general of volunteers, and as such served under the following governors: Mr. Eyre, Sir Henry Storks, and Sir J. P. Grant; appointed, by Sir H. Storks, commissioner to investigate and report on claims in connection with the late rebellion, to March, 1867; promoted to the rank of major, in the 1st West India regiment, 20th July, 1867; commanded the troops in the Gambia, 1868, 1869, during which time assisted the chief magistrate as a justice of the peace and commissioner of the court of requests; also acted as coroner; commanded the troops in British Honduras, and was a member of the executive and legislative councils, from 1871 to end of 1873; employed on the Frontier, on the occasion of the invasion of the Northern District by the Yucatec Indians of Yucatan, 1872; received the thanks of the lieutenant-governor for this service; also received the thanks of the inhabitants in a memorial sent through the governor, and on departure from British Honduras to join in the Ashanti expedition, was presented with a farewell address from the inhabitants of that colony; commanded the head-quarters of the 1st West India regiment during its advance across the Prah, with the advanced forces under major-general Sir Garnet Wolseley; promoted lieutenant-colonel, 24th December, 1873; on the withdrawal of the forces from the Gold Coast, succeeded to the command of the troops on the West Coast of Africa, and as such administered the government of the Gold Coast for a short time; member of the executive and legislative council of the Settlement of Sierra Leone.

JOHORE, MAHARAJAH OF.—His Highness Sir Datu Tummongong Abubakr Sri, K.C.S.L.; G.C.M.G. (1876).

JOLLIVET, ISIDORE.—District magistrate, Mauritius, February, 1862.

JONES, P.—Assistant treasurer, collector of stamps, and accountant-general supreme court, Penang; appointed clerk in treasury, March, 1861; promoted to be assistant treasurer, 1867.

JOSEPH, SIDNEY.—Appointed clerk in the office of the secretary of state for the colonies, July, 1843; was private secretary to Rt. Hon. Sir Jas. Stephen for seven years, and subsequently acted in the same capacity to Mr. Merivale for ten years; promoted assistant clerk, November, 1858; first class clerk, 30th September, 1872; Parliamentary clerk of the colonial office.

JUDGE, EDWARD ARTHUR.—Civil commissioner and resident magistrate of Queenstown division, Cape Colony; appointed December, 1858; was magistrate's clerk, Simon's Town, 1856 to 1857; clerk in Colonial Office, 1857 to 1861; acting C. C. and R. M., Namaqualand, 1861 to 1864; C. C. and R. M., Namaqualand, 1864 to 1869; inspector-general of chests, &c., 1875.

JULYAN, SIR PENROSE G., K.C.M.G. (1874), C.B. (1869).—Served as a volunteer during the Canadian rebellion in 1837-8; special commissioner of roads and bridges in Lower Canada in 1839; appointed to the commissariat in 1845. During the great immigration into Canada, which followed the Irish famine in 1847, was selected by the commander of the forces to organize, for the colony, an extensive quarantine establishment on Grosse Isle, in the river St. Lawrence, with a view of checking the terrible epidemic brought to that country by the emigrants. For the successful manner in which this service was performed, he was promoted by the Lords Commissioners of Her Majesty's Treasury to the rank of deputy-assistant commissary-general, and received the thanks of the colonial government. Was appointed assistant financial secretary to the board of works in Ireland in 1848; nominated director of a branch of the royal mint in Australia in 1852, and was employed on mint service until the war broke out with Russia, and was then recalled to the commissariat; was employed as an engineer during the early part of the war, and then designed and superintended the construction of a "Marine Steam Flour Mill" and a "Floating Bakery" for the supply of the army in the Crimea, which rendered valuable services throughout the war. For these and other inventions, which led to great economy and efficiency in army administration, received the special thanks of the Minister for War, and was promoted to the rank of assistant commissary-general, January 2, 1856; and created a C.B. in May, 1869. While in the commissariat, served in Great Britain, Ireland, North America, and the Mediterranean; was appointed crown agent for the colonies in 1858; sent on a special commission of
inquiry into the civil establishments and general expenditure of Mauritius, 1873.

JUMEAUX, ARTHUR.—Writer, Ceylon civil service, 1865; attached to Jaffna Katcheri, Feb. 1868; commissioner of requests, &c., Avisavila and Pasyalia, 1871; acting police magistrate, Matara, May, 1873.

KEENS, JAMES HENRY.—Formerly president of the privy council; assistant justice of the court of common pleas; member of the legislative council, 1845; and a member of the executive committee, Tobago; was master in chancery from 1837 to 1853; police magistrate from 1858 to 1856; administered government of Tobago for ten months in 1856 and 1857.

KEITH, W. G.—Appointed assistant colonial surgeon to government of Ceylon, 1870.

KELLY, L. F.—Appointed deputy assistant commissary-general at Trincomalee, Ceylon, 1862; appointed writer, Ceylon civil service, 1868, and attached to Colombo Katcheri.

KELLY, REV. WM. FRED., M.A.—Was colonial chaplain of Matelle, Ceylon; appointed by the Bishop of Colombo to the chaplaincy of Nuwara Eliya, 1864; colonial chaplain, St. Peter's church, 1871.

KELLY, RIGHT REV. JAMES B.—Educated at Clare College, Cambridge, B.A., 1854, M.A. 1858, and D.D. 1867; was formerly vicar of Kirk-Michael, Isle of Man, and chaplain to the Bishop of Sodor and Man; appointed arch-deacon of Newfoundland and Labrador, 1865; consecrated coadjutor bishop of Newfoundland, 1867.

KENDALL, CAPT. J. J.—Entered Her Majesty's 44th regiment as ensign, 28th August, 1854; appointed lieutenant, 9th March, 1855; captain, 31st December, 1858; served with the 44th regiment; served in the Crimea from 1st June, 1855, including the siege and fall of Sebastopol, and attacks on the Redan on the 8th and 18th of June (medal and clasps, and Turkish medal); served with a wing of the 1st battalion, 6th regiment, throughout the operations against the Hill tribe in Sikkim in 1861, and was in temporary command of the field force employed in that expedition during the absence of Lieut.-Col. Gawler, the brigadier; also held a command in the army of the late Emperor Maximilian in Mexico, from the year 1865, until the death of His Majesty, by whom he was decorated with the cross of "Guadaloupe" for distinguished service in the field at the battle of "Las Cruces," on which occasion he had two horses shot under him; appointed colonial secretary of Sierra Leone, in Sept. 1868; appointed administrator-in-chief of the West Africa settlements by a commission, dated 22nd April, 1869, and administered the government-in-chief from 15th Aug. to 8th Dec. 1869; administered the government of Sierra Leone on several subsequent occasions during the temporary absence of the governor; acted as police magistrate of Sierra Leone from 8th Aug. 1870 to April, 1871; again administered the government-in-chief during portions of the months of May and June, 1871.

KENNEDY, KT. BACHEL (1867), K.C.M.G. (1871), C.B. (1862), SIR ARTHUR EDWARD.—Educated at Trinity College, Dublin. Entered the army as ensign in the 11th regiment in 1827; lieutenant 1832; captain 68th light infantry, 1840; retired from the army in 1848 to accept civil employment; was selected (while serving in the army) in 1846 to fill the office of county inspector under the board of works; and served uninterruptedly during the Irish famine, as inspector under Sir John Burgoyne's relief commissioner; and subsequently as inspector of poor laws, till the office was abolished in 1851; appointed governor of the "Gambia," and transferred to Sierra Leone in 1852; consul-general of the adjoining Sherbro County, in 1854; and removed in the same year to the government of Western Australia; administered the latter government without interruption till February, 1862; created Companion of the Bath in 1862; appointed governor of Vancouver's Island, November, 1863; governor of the West Africa Settlements, November, 1867; and governor of Hong Kong, 1872; governor of Queensland, 1877.

KENNY, KT. BACHEL (Created 1870), SIR EDWARD KENNY.—Born 1800; sat in legislative council of Nova Scotia for 26 years, during 12 of which he was president of that body; called to the Senate, 1867; receiver-general, July, 1867; president of privy council, Oct. 1869; administrator of the government of Nova Scotia for several months in 1870.

KER, ALAN.—Called to the bar at the Middle Temple, Nov. 1842; chief justice of Nevis, 1854; appointed chief justice of Dominica, 1856; and assistant judge of the supreme court of Jamaica, 1861; acted as attorney-general of Antigua, from August, 1851, to March, 1854; member of legislative council, May, 1876.

KERR, THOMAS.—Was employed in the colonial secretary's department, Barbadoes, in 1856. Appointed police magistrate for the parish of St. Andrew, April, 1860; promoted to the parish of Christchurch, October, 1861, and to the city of Bridgetown, June, 1866; judge of the petty debt court of Bridgetown, Sept. 1869. Major of the 11th or St. Joseph's regiment militia, 1854; commanding officer since 1858. Represented the parish of St. Joseph in the house of assembly from 1862 to 1866. Member of council 1876.

KEYT, F.—Licentiate of medicine, Bengal College; medical assistant, Ceylon, 1863; assistant colonial surgeon, 1867.

KIDD, RICHARD HAYWARD, M.A.—Educated privately, and at Christ's College, Cambridge; deacon, 1862; priest, 1863, by Bishop of Norwich, curate of All Saints with St. Pileau, Norwich, 1862, 1863; incumbent of St. Benedict's, Norwich, 1863—1865; secretary of the Irish Society, 1866, 1867; rector of St. Michael Coslany, Norwich, 1867—1871; appointed colonial chaplain, Hong Kong, May, 1871; author of various published sermons, reports, and tracts.

KILLIKELLY, WM. EDW.—Educated for the army at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst. Was private secretary and aide-de-camp to his father during his administration of the government of St. Kitts in 1833; entered the service of the imperial customs at Demerara in 1835; promoted in same department to St. Kitts in 1836; where he continued to serve until 1844, when he was promoted to be comptroller and landing surveyor at Grenada; specially appointed to be acting collector at Grenada in 1845, and comptroller of navigation laws in 1849; appointed comptroller of colonial customs in 1855; was private secretary to Lieut.-Governor Kortright from June, 1859, to Jan. 1864; held the same appointment under Lieut.-Governor Mundy; is a justice of the peace, a member of assembly; aide-de-camp to the lieut.-governor; appointed police magistrate of the northern district, Grenada, Aug. 1865.

KIMBERLEY, 1ST EARL OF (United Kingdom), created 1866; BARON WODEHOUSE (Great Britain), 1797; baronet, 1811; privy councillor, 1864.—JOHN WODEHOUSE, son of the late Hon. Henry Wode-
house (who died in 1834) by the only daughter of Theophilus Thomhagh Gurdon, Esq., of Letton, Norfolk; born in London, 1826; married, 1847, the eldest daughter of the 3rd Earl of Clare; succeeded his grandfather in 1846; educated at Christ Church, Oxford, where he was 1st class in classics, 1847; was appointed a deputy-lieutenant of Norfolk, 1847; was under-secretary for foreign affairs from Dec. 1852, to April, 1856; envoy extraordinary and minister plenipotary to Russia from May, 1856, to March, 1858; again under-secretary for foreign affairs from June, 1859, to July, 1861; under-secretary of state for India, 1864; was lord privy seal, Dec. 1868, to July, 1870; secretary of state for the colonies, 6th July, 1870, to 20th Feb. 1874; has been a member of the senate of the University of London since 1859; sent on a special mission to Copenhagen, December, 1863; lord-lieutenant of Ireland from Oct. 1864, to June, 1866, when he was created an earl; is patron of eleven livings. The first baronet in this family had previously been knighted for his conduct at the siege of Cadiz; the 5th baronet represented Norfolk in five parliaments, and the 6th was the 1st Baron Wodehouse, and great grandfather of the present earl.

KING, CHARLES KEASLEY BERRY.—Educated at Stonyhurst College; matriculated at the London University, 1855; appointed 1st clerk and 3rd sub-immigration agent, British Guiana, 1st November, 1871; 2nd sub-immigration agent, 6th June, 1872; sub-immigration agent in charge of Berbice District, 1st January, 1875.

KING, J.E.A.—Appointed a writer in the Ceylon civil service, 1865, and in the same year acting police magistrate of Upper and Lower Doombera; acting assistant government agent, Kandy, 1866; commissioner of requests, &c., Harrispattu, 1866; acting assistant government agent, Nuwara Eliya, 1867; acting police magistrate, Gampola, Dec. 1867; district judge, &c., Badulla, 1868; acting assistant government agent, &c., Hambantota, 1870; district judge, Kegalla, Sept. 1872; assistant government agent, Kegalla, June, 1878; acting post-master-general, Oct. 1878.

KING, F. EUSTACE.—Clerk in the colonial secretary's office, Barbados, from May, 1866, to May, 1868; transferred from there to the government secretary's office, British Guiana, in June, 1868, and served there as clerk until December, 1870; inspector of police and justice of the peace, British Guiana, January, 1871; commissary of taxation, July, 1873, until 25th June, 1875, when he was appointed emigration agent at Barbados for British Guiana.

KING, FRANCIS OGLEBY.—Registrar of the county of Berbice, British Guiana; entered registrar's office of Demerara and Essequebo, British Guiana, as a clerk and copyist, on 1st April, 1858; appointed third assistant sworn clerk in said office on 28th January, 1860; second assistant sworn clerk on 21st July, 1860; and first assistant sworn clerk in June, 1862; acted as sworn clerk and notary public from 8th October, 1868, to 7th April, 1864; and again from 6th June to 29th August, 1867; appointed sworn clerk and notary public 12th February, 1868, after examination before the judges of the Supreme Court of Civil Justice of said colony; registrar of the county of Berbice, 7th July, 1868; justice of peace, and also commissioner for administering oaths to affidavits, 18th July, 1868; acted as sub-comptroller of customs and sub-comptroller of duties, and sub-book-keeper for the said county of Berbice from 1st of August to 31st October, 1872; special justice of peace, 11th June, 1875.

KING, H.—Appointed acting commissary tax-

tion, British Guiana, 1st July, 1865, to 30th June, 1866; magistrates' clerk, 1st August, 1867.

KING, H.G.—Clerk to auditor-general; clerk to commissioners for rebuilding the town of Basseterre, St. Kitts; provincial treasurer; appointed cashier and bookkeeper treasury department, 1873.

KING, J. HAMPDEN.—Graduated at Oxford; called to the bar at the Inner Temple, May, 1843; was a member of the house of assembly in Barbados from 1847 to 1853, and again in 1862; appointed a judge of the court of appeal at Barbados, 1858; acted as colonial secretary from April, 1860, to March, 1862; acted as auditor-general from March to May, 1862; appointed to administer the government of St. Kitts during the absence of Sir B.C.C. Pine, 6th August, 1862; second puisne judge, British Guiana, 1868. Acting chief justice, 1875-76.

KING, T.N.—Appointed assistant commissary of taxation, British Guiana, 25th June, 1874.

KINGSTON (JAMAICA), 1ST BISHOP OF. Founded 1856.—RIGHT REV. REGINALD COURTENAY, D.D.—Educated at Magdalen Hall, Oxford, where he graduated B.A., 1835, M.A. 1838; appointed arch-deacon of Middlesex in Jamaica in 1858; and co-adjutor to the Bishop of Jamaica, under the title of Bishop of Kingston, Feb. 1856; a privy councillor in Jamaica, Sept. 1856.

KIRKE, HENRY.—Graduated at Oxford B.A. 1863, M.A. 1866, B.C.L. 1866. Called to the bar, Inner Temple, January, 1868; went the Midland circuit; Derby and Birmingham sessions; appointed stipendiary magistrate, British Guiana, Sept. 1872; acting puisne judge in the same colony, April 7th, 1874.

KIRKWALL, VISCOUNT, K.C.M.G. (1875), (C.M.G. 1864).—Entered the army as an ensign in the 92nd Highlanders, Aug. 8, 1845; lieutenant, Nov. 9, 1846; captain, Nov. 1853; exchanged into the 71st Highland light infantry in 1854; served with that regiment in the trenches before Sebastopol; was at the taking of Kerch and Yanakale; received a medal and clasp for Sebastopol, and Turkish medal was granted March 2, 1858; Her Majesty's royal license and permission to accept and wear the insignia of the 5th class of the imperial order of the Medjidie, which his Imperial Majesty the Sultan was pleased to confer upon him, as a mark of his majesty's approbation of his distinguished services before the enemy in the late war. Served as aide-de-camp to Sir Henry Ward, G.C.M.G., then lord high commissioner in the Ionian Islands, from 1851 to 1854; appointed to the Scots Fusilier Guards in 1856; sold out of the army in 1857; is a deputy-lieutenant of Ayrshire, and a captain in the royal Bucks yeomanry cavalry; received the grand cross of St. Saviour from the king of the Hellenes, July, 1868.

KNIGHT, ARTHUR.—Appointed short-hand reporter to the legislative council of the Straits Settlements, 1st April, 1869; acting chief clerk, audit office, 6th September, 1869; chief clerk, same department, 21st October, 1873. Accompanied Governor Sir Harry Ord on his special mission to Labuan in 1873, and assisted in the investigation of the financial and commercial condition of that colony; acting assistant colonial secretary and clerk of councils, 14th May, 1875.

KNOLLYS, C.C.—Educated at Magdalen College, Oxford, where he gained an open scholarship in 1868; 1st class in mathematical moderations 1870; 2nd class in the final schools, 1872; B.A., 1873; appointed sub-receiver and harbour master at San Fernando, Trinidad, 1874.

KOCH, REV. C.A.—Appointed colonial chaplain, Jaffna, Ceylon, 1869.
KOCH, E. L.—Licentiate of medicine and surgeon, Bengal college; appointed medical assistant to Ceylon government, 1862; assistant colonial surgeon 1st class, 1867.

KORTRIGHT, CORNELIUS H.—Appointed a local magistrate at the Bahamas, 19 Feb., 1849; president administering the government of the Virgin Islands, 1854; lieut.-governor of Grenada, Nov. 1856; appointed to be lieut.-governor of Tobago, April, 1864; was acting governor, Trinidad, in 1868; appointed administrator of the government of the Gambia, 1873; governor of the West Africa Settlements, 1875; governor of British Guiana, 1877.

KRIEKENBEEK, C. A., M.D.—Appointed medical sub-assistant to the government of Ceylon; 3rd class, 1843; 2nd class, 1845; 1st class, 1854; assistant colonial surgeon, 1858; ditto, 1st class, 1867.

KRIEKENBEEK, C. I., M.B.C.M.—Appointed assistant colonial surgeon in the medical department, Ceylon, April, 1869.

KYNNERSLEY, C. W. SNEYD.—Appointed to the civil service, Straits Settlements, 1872; secretary assistant lieut.-governor's office, Penang, 1873.

KYSHB, J. B., F.S.S.—Assistant district clerk, Mauritius, 10th August, 1857; clerk, colonial secretary's office, 15th August, 1859; acting registrar, 15th March, 1860; financial and statistical clerk, 10th December, 1860; financial clerk and president of the stamping committee, 1st September, 1866; government translator, 22nd November, 1866; secretary, civil service enquiry commission, 4th December, 1868; secretary, Duke of Edinburgh's reception committee, 14th December, 1869; secretary, census commission, 12th May, 1870; secretary, census commission, 1st February, 1871; acting registrar-general, 4th June, 1872; acting secretary to councils of government, 14th July, 1873; financial and statistical clerk, C.S.O., 25th November, 1873 acting; secretary to councils of government 1st October, 1874.

LABASTIDE, LOUIS AUGUSTUS DE JACQUES DE, C.E.—Entered the public service at Trinidad on the 1st of July, 1869, in the office of public works; was appointed chief draughtsman on 1st January, 1870; graduated at the University of Paris; is a bachelor of science; gained the prize in high mathematics at St. Louis College, Paris; was then admitted a member of "special mathematics" society in that college; was admitted into the government engineering school "Ecole Impériale Centrale des Arts et Manufactures;" was admitted a sworn land surveyor in March, 1872.

LABORDE, EDWARD.—Colonial secretary and registrar-general, St. Vincent, appointed 1861; entered the colonial service as clerk in the treasury of that island, 1850; deputy treasurer, 1852; acting colonial secretary, 1856; police magistrate, 1857; stipendiary magistrate and coroner, 1858; provost-marshal, 1860; commanded, until 1868, the St. George's volunteers, which were raised by him in 1863; administered the government of Grenada in 1871; and that of St. Vincent in 1872; administered the government of Grenada again in 1874.

LABORDE, REV. H. W.—Rector of St. George's and St. Andrew's parishes, and chaplain of the gaol, St. Vincent, appointed 1852; M.A. Cambridge, where he graduated B.A., 1845; was ordained assistant curate in St. Vincent, 1845; was minister of All Saints' chapel and garrison, chaplain of the island of Trinidad, 1850 to 1852; is chaplain to the Bishop of Barbados; was appointed the rural dean of St. Vincent, 1864; and also a member of the legislative council.

LABUAN, 2nd Bishop of. Consecrated, July 29th, 1869.—RIGHT REV. DR. CHAMBERS.—For many years archdeacon of Sarawak.

LAIRD, DAVID.—Born 1838; sat in Prince Edward Island Assembly from 1871 to 1873, when returned to the dominion house of commons, where he still sits. Was a member of the executive council, P. E. I., from Nov. 1872, to April, 1873, and whilst holding that position negotiated for the entrance of the colony into the dominion; sworn of the privy council, and appointed minister of the interior of the dominion, 7th Nov., 1873; lieutenant-governor of the north-west territories, 7th Oct., 1876.

LAKE, ALEXANDER.—A solicitor in Jamaica; clerk of the peace for St. Mary's, and clerk of the St. Ann's district court, Jamaica.

LAMOND, G.—Appointed clerk in the audit office, Natal, 1859; and second clerk in the office of colonial secretary of that colony, 1859; 1st clerk, 1864.

LAMOTHE, CHAR.—Appointed inspector of distilleries at Mauritius, Jan. 1856; acting superintendent of same, September, 1862; superintendent, July, 1863.

LANDOR, E. W.—Appointed police magistrate, Perth, W. Australia, 1865.

LANE, COLONEL CECIL NEWTON, C.M.G. (1864).—Was a resident at Cephalonia until the cession of the Ionian Islands to the Kingdom of Greece.

LANG, WM. M.D.—Health officer, Carriacou, Grenada, 1863; medical officer, St. Andrew's parish, 1867.

LANGEVIN, EDOUARD JOSEPH, N.P.—Admitted as a notary public, Lower Canada, 3rd Dec., 1858; a member of board of notaries of Lower Canada for several years; appointed clerk of the Crown in Chancery, Canada, 4th Jan., 1865; to same office for dominion, 5th July, 1867; deputy registrar-general, 1st July, 1868; under secretary of state of Canada, 9th July, 1873; was major 9th Batt. V.M., or Voltigeurs de Quebec, and retired retaining rank, 1865.

LANGEVIN, HECTOR LOUIS, C.B. (1868), Q.C.—Born, 1826; called to the bar of Lower Canada, 1850; created a queen's counsel, 1864; mayor of Quebec from 1858 to 1861, and as such received H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his landing in Canada, 1860; entered Canadian parliament, 1857, and has almost uninterruptedly held a seat up to the present time, first in the old legislative assembly, and since confederation, in the house of commons of the dominion; appointed a member of the executive council, Canada, and solicitor-general for Lower Canada, 30th March, 1864; postmaster-general, Nov., 1866; at confederation, 1st July, 1867, sworn of the queen's privy council and appointed secretary of state of Canada; minister of public works, 8th Dec., 1869, and whilst holding that office was elected as the successor of the late Sir G. E. Cartier, Bart., as leader of the liberal conservative party of Lower Canada; resigned office, 5th Nov., 1873; was one of the framers of the present Canadian constitution, and in furtherance of the cause of confederation attended the colonial conferences at Charlottetown and Quebec in 1864, and in London in 1866, when the Act of Union was carried through the imperial parliament; created a Knight Commander of the Roman Order of St. Gregory the Great, 1870; is the author of a prize essay on Canada, and of several other works.

LANGTON, JOHN, M.A.—Sat in Canadian parliament from 1851 to 1855, when appointed auditor
of public accounts for province; appointed auditor of the dominion, 30th May, 1868; and subsequently, deputy of the minister of finance, and secretary of the treasury board; declined the finance ministry-ship, 1862; has been vice-chancellor of the University of Toronto.

LANYON, MAJOR W. OWEN, C.M.G., (1875).—Aide-de-camp to the major-general commanding the forces, Jamaica, Aug. 1865, till March, 1868; aide-de-camp to Sir J. P. Grant, K.C.B., governor of Jamaica, April, 1868; appointed private secretary, August, 1868; volunteered for service on Gold Coast 1873; for some time acted as colonial secretary; afterwards aide-de-camp to Sir G. Wolseley; despatched on special service to the Gold Coast to act as colonial secretary, November, 1874; sat in the executive and legislative councils; promoted to be a regimental major, April, 1874; administrator of the government, Grigualand West 1875.

LAURENCE, E. H.—Resident magistrate, Greenough, Western Australia, March, 1870; was clerk of councils, and private secretary to the acting governor, Nov. 1868, to Sept. 1869; clerk in governor's office and various departments from March, 1863.

LAURIE, ARCHIBALD CAMPBELL.—Appointed district judge of Kandy, July, 1873; is a member of the Faculty of Advocates of Scotland; called in 1860.

LAVERS, JAMES.—Appointed clerk in the customs at Mauritius, Oct. 1857; promoted, Feb. 1859; senior clerk, Sept. 1865.

LAWSON, W. T. G., C.E., &c., M.S.A., Assoc. G.N.A., &c., London.—Entered the service of colonial surveyors department, Sierra Leone, January, 1867; appointed assistant colonial surveyor for and one of the commissioners for crown land in British Sherbro, April, 1867; acting colonial surveyor for Sierra Leone, May to August, 1868; assistant colonial surveyor, 1869; appointed surveyor in charge of Cape Coast works, during the Ashanti expedition, 1873 to 1874; was nominated to survey and relay out the town of Elmina, bombarded during the disturbance, consequent upon the transfer in 1873; engaged in works connected with the transfer of the head-quarters from Cape Coast to Accra.

LAYARD, C. H.—Deputy assistant commissary, Galle, Ceylon, Nov. 1863; assistant colonial storekeeper, 1867; acted as superintendent of police, southern province, from July to Dec. 1872.

LAYARD, STR C. P., K.C.M.G. (1876), (C.M.G., 1871).—Was formerly at St. John's College, Cambridge; appointed extra-assistant in the colonial secretary's office in Ceylon, 1830; fiscal and magistrate at Jaffna, 1831; assistant to the collector of Colombo, 1832; assistant government agent and district judge, at Kalutara, 1836; assistant government agent and district judge, Negombo, 1837; district judge, Galle, 1839; district judge of Trincomalee, 1840; district judge of Galle, 1850; government agent, western province, 1851; held acting appointment of colonial secretary in conjunction with his own office of government agent for the western province from April to 30th June, 1869, and again from 6th April to 5th Sept. 1871.

LAYARD, EDGAR LEOPOLD, C.M.G., (1875).—Whilst Her Majesty's consul in Fiji, was concerned in the negotiations which resulted in the cession of the islands to Great Britain; administered the government from the cession, in 1874, until the arrival of Sir A. Gordon, in 1875.

LEAKE, SIR LUKE SAMUEL, KNT. BACH. (1876).—Speaker of the legislative council, Western Australia.

LEARY, SAMUEL.—New Amsterdam, British Guiana; diploma of the College of Physicians, Dublin, 1860; diploma of the Faculty of Physicians and Surgeons, Glasgow, 1855; diploma in Midwifery, Andersonian University, 1852, and Faculty Hall, Glasgow, 1855; J.P. and coroner, British Guiana; medical officer East Canje District, Berbice; surgeon, New Amsterdam jail and police health officer, Port of New Amsterdam; entered government service, 1st July, 1873; late medical officer, Skeldon District, Coventyne, Co., Berbice, 1867 to 1873; Philadelphian District, West Coast, Demerara, 1873 to 1875; surgeon, ship, "Caroline Coventry," Africa, East Indies and China, 1855 to 1857; Pettijo and Clonelly Dispensary Districts, Co. LEE, PERCY, M.R.C.S.E.—Appointed assistant colonial surgeon, Ceylon, 1868.

LEES, C. C., C.M.G. (1876).—Was private secretary and aide-de-camp to the governor-in-chief of the Leeward Islands, had local rank of lieut.-colonel, and brigade-major to the militia; entered the army in June, 1854; appointed adjutant to the 2nd battalion Royal Welch Fusiliers on its formation in 1858; sold out in Jan. 1866; and was appointed to the adjutancy of the 3rd administrative battalion Derbyshire rifle volunteers; resigned in May, 1867; appointed collector of customs, Lagos, Nov. 1872; administrator of the government of Lagos, July, 1874, and also lieutenant-governor of the Gold Coast Colony, Nov. 1874; administered the general government, 1876.

LEFEVRE, K.C.B. (Civil). (Cret. 1857.) SIR JOHN GEORGE SHAW LEFEVRE.—Educated at Eton and Trinity College, Camb., where he was senior wrangler, 1818; fellow of Trinity, 1819; graduated M.A. 1821; called to the bar at the Inner Temple, 1824; elected a bencher, 1855; appointed under-secretary of state for the colonies, 1833; poor-law commissioner, 1834; joint-assistant secretary to the board of trade, 1841; deputy-clerk of the parliaments, 1848; clerk of the parliaments, 1858; is an ecclesiastical commissioner, and vice-chancellor of the university of London; was a civil service commissioner, but resigned 1862.

LE FEUVRE, W. S.—Ensign Hampshire militia, 1858; lieutenant Hampshire militia (ombodied), 1854; ensign 77th regiment, 1854; lieutenant 77th regiment, 1855; assistant instructor, Hythe School of Musketry, 1855; instructor of musketry to 2nd brigade light division, Crimea, 1855-6; thanked in general orders; adjutant 77th regiment, 1856; resigned 1857; captain 2nd Hants volunteer rifles, 1860; secretary municipal council Kandy, Ceylon, 1866-73; acting superintendent of police, central province, Ceylon, 1871-1873; superintendent of police, head-quarters, Colombo; northern, eastern
and north-western provinces, Ceylon; also in charge of police stores, and pay departments, 1873.

LEFROY, A. O'GRADY.—Appointed treasurer of Western Australia, 1856; was private secretary to Governor Fitzgerald, 1849 to 1855; acting colonial secretary, 1875.

LEFROY, MAJOR-GENERAL JOHN HENRY, R.A., C.B. (Civil, 1870), F.R.S., &c.—Entered the Royal Artillery, 1834; director of the magnetical and meteorological observatory at St. Helena, 1840-1; at Toronto, 1842-1853; made a magnetic survey of the interior of the continent of North America from Montreal to the Arctic Circle, 1843-4; appointed to the War office as scientific adviser to the Duke of Newcastle on subjects of artillery and inventions, Dec. 1854; sent on special mission to the seat of war, Oct. 1855; and to the Mediterranean fortresses, March, 1859; inspector-general of army schools, 1857-9; secretary ordnance select committee, 1859-63; president, 1864-8; director-general of ordnance, 1868-70; honorary secretary royal commission of the Patriotic Fund, 1854-68; commissioner, 1868; was also a member of the royal commission on national defences, 1859; and on military education, 1868; appointed governor of Bermuda, 1871.

LEGGE, E.—Appointed clerk to hospital at San Fernando, Trinidad, 1873.

LEWIS, ALBERT, barrister-at-law.—Called to the bar Middle Temple; police and stipendiary magistrate and coroner, Grenadines, St. Vincent; appointed 1856; first appointment as deputy-provost marshal in 1849; left the service in 1869; temporarily re-entered it in May, 1870, and acted as police and stipendiary magistrate and coroner for the Kingstown police district, St. Vincent, until November, 1870, when he resumed practice at the bar; acted for the attorney-general of St. Vincent during his vacation leave at the end of 1873.

LEWIS, ALLAN.—Was clerk in the colonial secretary's office, St. Vincent, 1845; immigration agent, 1848 to 1857; deputy registrar of deeds, 1854; appointed police and stipendiary magistrate and coroner in that colony, 1860; colonial registrar, 1872; acting police magistrate, Kingstown district, 1874.

LEWIS, J. W.—Collector of customs, South Australia.

LOVÉSY, CONWAY WHITHORNE, of Queen's College, Oxford, M.A.—Was called to the bar, Middle Temple, 1845; editor of "Archbold's Practice of Quarter Sessions," and "Jervis on the Law of Coroners," and author of "The Churchwarden's Guide," "The Law of Arbitration between Masters and Workmen," and other legal works. LOW, WILLIAM.—Acting private secretary to Lieut.-Governor Longden at Dominica, June, 1866, to March, 1867; private secretary to Lieutenant-Governor Bulwer and clerk of the patents, April, 1867, to January, 1869; and to Lieut.-Governor Freeling from February to July, 1869, acted as colonial secretary of Dominica, 1868; police magistrate in St. Vincent, May, 1874.

LOWCOCK, HENRY.—Member of the legislative council, Hong Kong, 1875.

C.—Private secretary to the president of Turks Islands 1849; was also a member of the board of education, and honorary secretary and treasurer of the same; was a justice of the peace, and captain and adjutant in the Turks Islands volunteer corps; colonial secretary, April, 1866, and a member of executive council, March, 1867; appointed receiver-general and treasurer, Bahamas, 1873.

LOWTHER, JAMES, M.P.—Born 1840. Educated at Westminster School and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he graduated B.A., 1862, and M.A., 1866; called to the bar at the Inner Temple, 1864; is a magistrate and deputy lieutenant for the North Riding of York; was parliamentary secretary to the poor law board from August to December 1868; appointed parliamentary under-secretary for the colonies, February, 1874. First elected for the city of York, July, 1865.

LUCAS, G. A.—Was a captain in the 73rd regiment; appointed resident magistrate, Lower Umcomas, Natal, 1859; magistrate Klip River in that colony, 1860, and at Alexandra, 1875.

LUDLOW, HENRY.—Called to the bar, Lincoln's Inn, January, 1862; attained studentship, 1861. Employed in Friendly Society's commission, and also under the parliamentary counsel; attorney-general, Trinidad, May, 1874.

MAARTENSZ, A. G.—Medical practitioner, 1860; medical assistant to government of Ceylon, 1861; assistant colonial surgeon, 1867.

MACALISTER, ARTHUR, C.M.G. (1876).—Formerly colonial secretary and premier of Queensland, now agent-general for the colony in London.

MACARTHUR, KNT. BACHEL (creat. 1856).—SIR WILLIAM MACARTHUR.—Was an elective member of the legislative council of New South Wales from 1848 to 1855; resigned his seat to proceed as special commissioner from New South Wales to attend the universal exhibition at Paris; received the decoration of the legion of honour; is author of a treatise on the Cultivation of Vineyards and the Art of making Wine.

M'CINTOCK, WM. C. H.—Superintendent of river and creeks, Pomeroon, British Guiana.

MACBRIDE, R.—Superintending officer, public works department, Ceylon, 1866.

MACDONALD, SIR JOHN ALEXANDER, K.C.B., D.C.L. (Oxon); LL.D., Q.C., Kingston, P.C.—A member of the ex-council of Canada from May 1847 to March 1848; from September 1854 to July 1858, and from August same year to May 1862, and from March 1864 until the Union, was during these periods receiver-general; from May to December, 1847, commissioner of crown lands; 1847 to March, 1848, attorney-general; from September 1854 to July 1858, when, as prime minister, he and his cabinet resigned on being defeated on the seat of government question; returned to office on 6th August same year; resigned on the following day on his re-appointment as attorney-general, which he continued to hold until the defeat of the administration on the Militia Bill in May, 1862; again attorney-general in 1864, and led the assembly from that time until the union of the British American provinces, 1867; was chairman of the London colonial conference, 1866, 1867; when the act of Union was passed by the imperial parliament on the introduction of the new constitution in July 1867, was called upon to form the first government for the new Dominion; was sworn a privy councillor, and appointed minister of justice and attorney-general of Canada; in 1871 was appointed one of H.M. joint high commissioners, together with Earl de Grey, Sir S. Northcote, Sir E. Thornton, and Mr. Bernard, for the settlement of the Alabama claims, and all matters in dispute between Great Britain and the United States, resulting in the Treaty of Washington of 1871. Eldest son of the late Hugh Macdonald, Esq., of Kingston, Ontario, and formerly of Sutherlandshire, Scotland, born in 1815; educated at the royal grammar school, Kingston, under Dr. Wilson, a Fellow of Oxford University; married (1st) Isabella, daughter of the late Alexander Clark, Esq., of Dalnavert, Inverness-
shire, Scotland, she died in 1850; (2nd) 1867, Susan Agnes, daughter of the late Mr. T. T. Bernard, a member of H.M. privy council of the island of Jamaica; called to the bar, in Hilary term, 1838; created queen's councillor in 1846.

MAC-DONNELL, K.C.M.G. (1871), KNIGHT BACHEL (1855), C.B. (Civil 1852), SIR RICHARD GRAVES MAC-DONNELL.—Entered Trinity College, Dublin, 1830; gained several honours both in classics and science when an undergraduate; obtained a scholarship in 1833; graduated B.A. 1835, M.A. 1838, hon. L.L.D. 1844; called to the bar in Ireland, 1838, and at Lincoln's Inn, 1840; was chief justice of the Gambia from 1843 to 1847; governor of that colony from 1847 to 1851; conducted several exploring expeditions up the Gambia, and in the interior of Africa between that river and the Senegal; appointed governor of St. Lucia, 1852, and transferred to St. Vincent same year; governor of South Australia, 1855, until March, 1862; governor of Nova Scotia, April, 1864; governor of Hong Kong, 14th Oct., 1865. Retired on pension, 1872.

McCLOSKY, JAMES HUGH, J.P.—Colonial Surgeon, Labuan, 1871; member of legislative council; entered the colonial service in 1859 late assistant-surgeon in Her Majesty's Indian army; served in the Indian campaign during mutiny in India, 1857-58 (medal).

MACCLURE, DR. W. M. G.—Appointed physician to prison and police, and health officer, Bahamas, 1873.

MCCULLOCH, KNT. BACHEL (United Kingdom, creat. 1870), K.C.M.G. (1874).—SIR JAMES McCulloch.—Was chief secretary to the executive government of Victoria, and in that capacity was premier of the ministry; resigned, 1872.

McEWEN, E. JAMES.—Appointed clerk to provost marshal, Grenada, January, 1868; colonial revenue officer, June, 1871.

McEWEN, J. P.—Entered the royal navy, 1855; served in the Baltic campaign of that year in H.M.S. 'Hastings,' 60 guns, and was present at the attack on the Sandham forts at the bombardment of Helsingfors; served on the East and West Coasts of Africa in the suppression of the slave trade; was in the Niger expedition of 1864, and succeeded in ascending the Tchenchegga River in H.M.S. 'Investigator,' to within 9 miles of Bida; received a letter of thanks from the Admiralty, and one from the hydrographer, for services rendered on that occasion, and was also promoted to navigating lieutenant; was appointed to command H.M. colonial steamer 'Corra Linne,' on the West Coast of Africa, September, 1866, and afterwards to H.M. coast steamer 'Sherbro'; was appointed a commissioner under the foreign office for the settlement of the Liberian boundary question; served on the Gold Coast during a part of the Ashantee campaign, and on a mission to the Gambia in search of troops; on the return of the 'Sherbro' to England, was appointed to the command of H.M. colonial steamer 'Pluto,' in the Straits Settlement; resigned, April, 1875; assistant harbour-master, Hong Kong.

MAC GEE, W. J.—Extra clerk, colonial office, April, 1863; clerk in the registry department, Mar. 1864; clerk in the general department, July, 1870.

MACKGLASHAN, JOHN CHAS.—Chief clerk in the office of the colonial secretary, Jamaica; is also clerk of the privy council; was appointed clerk in executive committee office, in June, 1856; was, in April, 1866, on the death of the secretary to the executive committee and clerk, privy council, appointed provisionally to those offices, pending the change in the constitution of the island, under which it became a crown colony; held those appointments until the inauguration of the new form of government; then appointed chief clerk in the financial secretary's office; and in the amalgamation of that office in February, 1870, with the colonial secretariat, appointed chief clerk in the latter office; acted as assistant colonial secretary from April to October, 1870, and again from June to December in 1871; acting auditor-general from September 1872, to January 1873; acting assistant colonial secretary, January, 1873 acting colonial secretary, February, 1873; acting assistant, June, 1873; acting colonial secretary, 28th August, 1873; January, 1874; and acting assistant, July, 1874; auditor-general, 1875.

McDOUGALL, W., C.B.—Born 1822; admitted as an attorney of Upper Canada, 1847; called to the bar, 1862; for many years on the daily political press of Toronto; sat in Canadian parliament from 1858 up to 1872; is now a member of the Ontario assembly; appointed commissioner of crown lands, 24th May, 1862; provincial secretary, 31st June, 1864; minister of public works of the dominion, 1st July, 1867; lieut.-governor of Rupert's land and the north-west territories, October, 1869; was a special commissioner to England on several occasions, most notably in connection with confederation, the acquisition of the north-west territories, immigration, and on the subject of defence.

McGILL, E. F.—Appointed clerk in the surveyor-general's office, Natal, 1845, and clerk and draughtsman in the civil engineers' department of that colony, 1860; chief clerk and accountant, 1865.

McHA'TTIE, A. G., M.D., M.R.C.S., ENGLAND.—Medical officer district No. 2, Antigua.

MACKENZIE, HON. ALEXANDER.—Born near Dunkeld, Perthshire, 28th January, 1822. Educated at the public schools of Moulin, Dunkeld, and Perth. Married, 1st, Helen, daughter of the late Mr. Wm. Neil, of Irvine, Scotland (she died 2nd January, 1852); 2ndly, 17th June, 1853, Jane, eldest daughter of the late Mr. Robert Sym, of Perthshire, Scotland. In youth learned the business of a builder and architect, and after arrival in Canada, became a contractor. For some years edited the 'Lambton Shield,' a reform journal. Is president of the isolated risk and fire insurance company; and a commissioner ex officio to assist Mr. Speaker in the management of the interior economy of the house of commons. Was major 27th Lambton battalion of volunteer infantry, for some years up to October, 1874, when he resigned. Was a member of executive council, and treasurer of Ontario (in Mr. Blake's administration), from 21st December, 1871, until October, 1872, when he retired with Mr. Blake for the purpose of devoting themselves entirely to Dominion politics. Declined a seat in the Canadian cabinet, on the occasion of the retirement of Mr. Brown, 1865. Was leader of Ontario reform opposition in house of commons from the union until 1873, when chosen leader of the whole opposition party, and continued in that position until 5th November, 1873, when, owing to the resignation of Sir John Macdonald, he was called upon to form a new administration, a duty he succeeded in accomplishing on 7th of the same month, when he and his colleagues were sworn of the privy council, he (Mr. Mackenzie) taking the office of minister of public works. Proceeded to the mother country on public business, June, 1875, and while there was presented with the freedom of Irvine, Dundee, and Perth. Sat for Lambton in Canada assembly from 1861 until the union. Returned to house of commons at general election, 1867; and at general election, 1872, re-elected by acclamation.
on his appointment to office, and again at last general election. Represented West Middlesex in Ontario assembly from general election, 1871, until October, 1872, when he resigned. Several important public measures owe their existence to Mr. Mackenzie, as a private member, viz.: the act amending the assessment act of Upper Canada (1863); that consolidating and amending the acts relating to the assessment of property, Upper Canada (1866); and the highly useful measure for providing means of egress from public buildings (1866). As chairman of committee on municipal and assessment laws (1866), wrote and framed the greater part of the general act on municipal corporations, &c. All the measures of his government, including the enactment of a stringent election law, with the trial of election petitions by judges, and vote by ballot; the abolition of the real estate qualification of members; the inspection of produce and weights and measures; the better administration of penitentiaries; the enactment of the marine telegraph law, which virtually abolishes the monopoly of the cable company; the establishment of a Dominion military college, and the improvement of the militia system; the enlargement of the canals; the permanent organization of the civil service; the establishment of a supreme court for the Dominion; the reduction of postage to and from the United States; the free delivery of postal matter in cities and towns; the opening of direct mail communication with the West Indies; the construction of a transcontinental telegraph line; the better administration of Government railways; an improved copyright law; a new insolvent law; and the establishment of a territorial government for the great North-West, have all been more or less his work. In addition, two very important questions, which for some time agitated the public mind and threatened the gravest complications—the Manitoba amnesty and the New Brunswick school questions—have been satisfactorily adjusted during Mr. Mackenzie's administration.

MACKENZIE, REV. D. C.—Chaplain, Kandian District, Ceylon.

McKINNEY, W. J.—Postmaster of British Honduras; appointed 1859; is secretary to the council for education; served as an ensign in the Belize volunteers, under Captain Edmunds, late 4th W.I. regt. on the northern frontier of the colony in 1866-67, against the hostile Indians of Yucatan; was mentioned in despatches, and received the thanks of the legislative assembly for his services acting police magistrate, 1875.

MACKINNON, WILLIAM F.—Entered the service as a 3rd class clerk in the financial secretary's office, August, 1867; 2nd class clerk, April, 1875; travelling supervisor of post offices, 1876.

McKINSTY, T. W.—Chief Clerk, colonial secretary's office, Barbados, appointed 1872; served many years in the commissariat department in British North America and in the West Indian islands; retired from the army as assistant commissary-general in 1870, receiving the commutation allowance.

MACLEAN, C. R.—Acting stipendiary magistrate of the 4th judicial district, from 20th June, 1862, to 23rd June, 1863, St. Lucia. In Dec., 1863, again acted as special justice of the 4th district, in which appointment he was afterwards confirmed; in Nov., 1867, removed from the 4th to the 1st judicial district; performed also the duties of coroner, visiting justice of the Royal gaol, and district road commissioner, until the latter office was abolished in 1871; in March, 1868, was appointed official member of the legislative council, and in March, 1871, appointed chairman of the poor law committee of the 1st district.

MACLEAN, SIR DONALD, K.C.M.G. (1874).—Minister for native affairs, New Zealand; appointed to be a companion of the Order of St. Michael and St. George in 1870, and promoted to be a Knight commander of that Order in 1874.

MACLEAR, KNT. BACHEL (Creet. 1860.)—SIR THOS.—Astronomer-royal at the Cape.

MACLEAY, SIR GEORGE, K.C.M.G. (1875), (C.M.G. 1869).—Eldest surviving son of the late Alexander Macleay, Esq., for many years secretary to the transport board, and subsequently colonial secretary and first speaker of the legislative assembly of New South Wales; was educated at Westminster; went at an early age to New South Wales; accompanied in 1829-30, Captain Sturt on his expedition down the river Murrumbidgee and Murray, and was for several years a member of the legislature of New South Wales.

MACLURE, DR. WM. M. G.—Coroner, Nassau, N.L., Bahamas, 1865; appointed physician to prison, police force and health officer, 1873; member of legislative assembly since 1866.

MACMAHON, SIR CHARLES, KNT. BACH, (1875).—Speaker of the legislative assembly, Victoria.

MADAR, A. R.—Clerk in the treasury, Hong Kong, 1867.

McNAIR, J. F. A., MAJOR, R.A. (late Madras).—Is a cadet of 1845; served with his battery in India until 1850, and in the Straits Settlements, and Labuan from 1853 to 1857; appointed private secretary to the governor Straits Settlements, and subsequently executive engineer and superintendent of convicts; returned to Europe in 1865; employed under surveyor-general of prisons in the erection of the Woking female prison; appointed chief engineer and controller of convicts, Straits Settlements, on their transfer to the crown in 1867; acted as colonial secretary in 1868; appointed surveyor-general, 1872; is a member of both executive and legislative councils; Associate Institution of Civil Engineers, F.L.S., F.R.G.S., F.A.S.

MCNEILL, COLONEL JOHN CARSTAIRS, C.B., (1874), C.M.G. (1870), V.C.—Served during the campaign of 1857-58 in India as aide-de-camp to Sir F. Lugard during the siege and capture of Lucknow; in 1861, proceeded with Sir D. Cameron to New Zealand as his aide-de-camp, and served there until 1865; commanded the Tipperary flying column during the Fenian disturbances in the winter of 1866-67; served on the staff of the Red River expedition from Canada under Sir Garnet Wolseley, in 1870, and again under that officer in the Ashanti war, 1873-4; appointed an equerry in ordinary to Her Majesty, 1 Aug., 1874.

MAC VICAR, H. J.—Employed on the unfixed establishment of the surveyor-general's department, Ceylon, from June, 1870; assistant surveyor, October, 1871.

MAGALHAENS, JOZE MARIA RODRIGUES.—Appointed in 1848 as overseer to superintend the preparing of the granite stones for the construction of the Horsburgh Lighthouse; in 1850 was transferred to convict department up to 1854, during which time had charge of the House of Correction, superintended all the works both civil and military, and was transferred again to the Horsburgh Lighthouse; about 1854 was recalled and promoted to be head overseer, had charge of the town and country roads divisions; assisted to superintend all the military works in town, Mount Faber, and Mount Palmer, and was posted at the Rabbit and Coneys, during the construction of the Raffles Lighthouse; about 1858 was promoted again to be assistant
supervisor, and ordered to take charge of the works during the construction of the Field Fortress, Port Canning; after completion, returned to the town division and assisted in preparing the granite courses for the Alguada Lighthouse; in 1863 was transferred to Penang to take charge of Province Wellesley, and after eight months, recalled to take charge of the Singapore town division; in 1864 was promoted to be supervisor, in 1866 transferred to take charge of the Penang Division of Province Wellesley; in 1867 promoted to be assistant engineer.

MAINWARING, A.—Writer in the Ceylon civil service, Dec., 1865; acting commissioner of requests, and police magistrate, Harispatu; joint police magistrate, Kurunegalla, 1866; commissioner of requests, Harispatu, 1867; landing and tide surveyor, Galle, 1868; district judge, &c., Negombo, May, 1870; acting district judge, Kegalla, January, 1872.

MAIS, C. HENRY.—Appointed engineer-in-chief, South Australia, 1867. In addition to above, general manager of railways, 1867 to June, 1869; manager of railways from June, 1870.

MALCOLM, WILLIAM ROLLE.—Educated at Eton and Balliol College, Oxford; first class moderations, 1860, first class final classical examination, 1862; elected fellow of All Souls, 1864; called to the bar, L.I., 1865; secretary public schools commission, 1868; assistant secretary Board of Trade, 1870; appointed an assistant under secretary colonial office, 24 July, 1874.

MANNING, KNT. BACHEL (Creet. 1858).—Sir WILLIAM MONTAGU MANNING, LL.D.—Educated at Tavistock, at Southampton, and at University College, London; called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn, 1832; was chairman of quarter sessions in New South Wales from Oct., 1837 to Oct., 1844; solicitor-general from Oct., 1844 to Jan., 1848; acting judge of the supreme court from Jan., 1848 to Nov., 1849; again solicitor-general from Nov., 1849 to May, 1856; attorney-general from May, 1856, to May, 1858; is a member of the executive council of New South Wales, and one of the queen's counsel there; author of 'Notes of Proceedings in Electoral Revision Courts,' 'Nevile and Manning's Reports in Court of King's Bench,' 1832 to 1837.

MARTIN, KNT. BACHEL (Creet. 1869).—Q.C., Sir James Martin. Born 1820; educated at Sydney College, New South Wales; was called to the bar of New South Wales 1856 (having been for some time previously an attorney of the supreme court); appointed a queen's counsel there in 1857. Was five times attorney-general of New South Wales between 1856 and 1872, during four years of which time he filled the office of premier. Elected a member of the Senate of Sydney University Aug., 1858. Appointed chief justice of New South Wales, 1873.

MARTIN, HENRY D.—Harbour-master, Grenada; appointed 1860.

MATHEWS, THOMAS MARTIN.—Entered the Bahamas service as clerk in the police office, and held that appointment for upwards of twelve years; was admitted to the bar in Easter term, 1833; held for many years the appointment of assistant clerk to the house of assembly, and afterwards that of chief clerk; was appointed a lieutenant of militia in 1834, and in the year 1836 became military secretary to the commander-in-chief; was a member of the house of assembly for many years; was appointed judge advocate of militia in the year 1840; held the appointment of acting attorney-general in 1850; and in the same year was appointed member of the executive council. In 1852 was appointed on two occasions judge of the general court; in 1853, again acted as attorney-general and advocate and procurator-general in admiralty; again held those appointments in the years 1856 and 1860; held the appointment of acting judge of the court of common pleas on three occasions in the years 1874 and 1875; in the latter year was appointed queen's counsel and acting chief justice; legislative councillor, 1876.

MAURITIUS, 4th Bishop of, Peter Sorenson, Royston.—Trinity College, Cambridge, B.A. in classical and mathematical honours, 1853; M.A., 1860; D.D., 1872; resident tutor of Church Missionary College, 1853-55; corresponding secretary of South India mission, 1855-71, except from 1864-66, when incumbent of Plains Wilhems, Mauritius; consecrated 1872.

MAXSE, Lieut.-Colonel H. F. BERKELEY, C.M.G. MEADE, HONORABLE ROBERT HENRY.—Is an M.A. of Exeter College, Oxford; passed an examination before the civil service commissioners, May 9th, 1859; was appointed a junior clerk in the foreign office, June 1st, 1859; was attached to Lord Dufferin's special mission to Syria, from July 31, 1860, till Sept. 1861; accompanied the Prince of Wales during His Royal Highness's tour in the East, Germany, and Italy, in 1862; accompanied Earl Russell to Germany when his lordship was in attendance on Her Majesty, in the autumn of 1862; and accompanied Earl Granville to Germany on a similar occasion, in 1863, and again in 1865; was appointed groom of the bedchamber to H.R.H. the Prince of Wales, Nov. 27th, 1862; and was private secretary to Earl Granville, from June, 1864, till July, 1866; private secretary to Lord Granville when secretary of state for the colonies, from 9th Dec. 1868, till July, 1870, and when secretary of state for foreign
