ROSE, SIR JOHN, BART. (1872) K.C.M.G. (1870).—Was called to the bar of Lower Canada in 1842, and obtained a patent as Queen's counsel in 1847. In the year 1857 he accepted the position of solicitor-general of Canada, and was elected to parliament for the city of Montreal. Among the measures introduced by him as solicitor-general was that for the abolition of the Usury Laws. He became receiver-general of Canada in August, 1858, and afterwards minister of public works in 1859. In that capacity he had the control of the arrangements during the visit of His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales to Canada, and in the following year, until his resignation, those for His Royal Highness Prince Alfred. In 1867, at the first election of the Dominion parliament, he selected the county of Huntingdon, for which he was elected. The finance minister having resigned at the opening of the first session, that office, with a seat in the privy council, was accepted by him in November, 1867. He was requested by the governor-general, on behalf of Her Majesty's government, to make a confidential examination into the alleged grievances of the province of Nova Scotia to the financial terms conceded to that province in entering the union, and for a redress of which they had appealed to the Imperial Parliament. He gave it as his opinion that there were grounds for the complaints of Nova Scotia, and he recommended the extending of large financial concessions to them. He was selected in 1869 to proceed to Washington to confer with the government of the United States on the subject of reciprocal trade, the question of the fisheries, copyright, patent laws, &c., &c.; the navigation of the St. Lawrence, and extradition of criminals. In 1864 he was named by Her Majesty commissioner on the part of Great Britain, under the convention with the United States of America, of July, 1863, for the settlement of claims arising out of the Oregon Treaty of 1846, the duties of which were brought to a close in September, 1869. He resigned the office of minister of finance of Canada in October, 1869.

ROSS, A. C.—Clerk of the legislative council, and confidential clerk in the colonial secretary's office, Trinidad; entered the service in February, 1864.

ROSS, DAVID PALMER, M.D. Edin., M.R.C.S. Eng.—Chief medical officer and director, public hospital, Jamaica, 14th May, 1870; served formerly on the army medical staff; appointed parochial medical attendant, Spanish Town, 1866; medical superintendent, Cooly depot, 1867; a government medical officer, December, 1868; acted from December, 1868, to August, 1869, as resident medical officer and registrar, public hospital, in the room of two medical officers; medical superintendent, lepers' home, from February to May, 1870.

ROSTANT, LEONARD.—Appointed warden of the Couva ward union, 1st October, 1854; warden of North Paraima ward union, 1st June, 1866; justice of the peace for the county of Victoria, 1866; supervisor of excise, 14th September, 1869.

ROUILLARD, JOHN.—District magistrate, Mauritius, February, 1865.

ROUND, FRANCIS R., B.A.—Educated at Marlborough and Balliol College, Oxford, where he obtained a double second class in moderations, and a second in classics in the final examination, 1868; appointed, after a competitive examination, clerk in the office of the secretary of state for the colonies, February, 1869; 2nd class clerk, 30th September, 1872; accompanied Sir P. Julyan, K.C.M.G., C.B., to Mauritius in 1873 as secretary on the occasion of that gentleman's special commission of inquiry into the civil establishment and general expenditure of that colony.

ROWE, SAMUEL, C.M.G. (1874), Surgeon-Major.—Engaged on the West Coast of Africa since 1862 and as medical officer and chief of the staff with Sir J. H. Glover during the Ashante war, 1873-4, in which capacity he accompanied Sir J. H. Glover's force into Ashanti and through Coomassie; despatched on special service to the Gold Coast, November, 1874; lieutenant-governor, West Africa Settlements, 1875; administrator of the Gambia.
1875; conducted two expeditions into the Sherbro country in 1876; governor of the West Africa Settlements, 1876.

ROZARIO, RAFAEL A.—Appointed interpreter to the supreme court, Hong Kong, 1857.

RUPERT'S LAND, 2nd Bishop of. Appointed 1865.—RIGHT REV. ROBERT MACHRAY, D.D.—Late dean and fellow of Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, and vicar of Madingley; graduated in 1855, when he was 34th wrangler. The diocese of Rupert's Land is 37,000 square miles in extent; and has a population of 200,000 souls, and comprehends the whole of the Hudson's Bay Company's settlements (or Prince Rupert's Land); it was erected into a see in 1849, and endowed by a legacy from the late W. Leith, Esq.

RUSHWORTH, EDW. EVERARD, C.M.G. (1872).—D.C.L. and late fellow of St. John's College, Oxford; appointed a clerk in the inland revenue office, Somerset House, 1842; was private secretary to Sir Gaspard Le Marchant, in the governments of Newfoundland and Nova Scotia, from 1847 to 1855; president administering the government of Montserrat from 1855 to 1861; auditor-general of Mauritius, 1861. Was acting director of the railway department; a member ex officio of the council, and commissioner of admiralty court in that island; appointed March, 1866, government secretary, British Guiana; administrator, government of Trinidad, April, 1866; financial secretary, Jamaica, Oct. 1866; administered the government of Jamaica during Sir J. P. Grant's six months' absence in 1870; administered the government of British Guiana during the absence of Governor Scott in 1873.

RUSSELL, THE VERY REV. A.—Dean of Adelaide.

RUSSELL, EARL (creat. first Earl, Aug., 1861) G.C.M.G. (1869).—JOHN RUSSELL.—Was M.P. for Tavistock from 1813 till Mar. 1817, and also from July, 1818, till March, 1819; for Huntingdonshire from 1820 till 1826; and for Bandon Bridge from January, 1827, till 1830; was made a privy councillor, November 22, 1830; paymaster of the forces from December 16, 1830, till December 23, 1834; M.P. for Tavistock from December, 1830, till Dec. 1832, when he was returned for South Devon, which county he represented till May, 1835; appointed one of the ecclesiastical commissioners for England, Aug. 15, 1836; secretary of state for the home department from April 18, 1835, till Aug. 30, 1839; M.P. for Stroud from May 21, 1835, till June, 1841; secretary of state for the colonies from Aug. 30, 1839, to Sept. 3, 1841; M.P. for the city of London, from July, 1841, to 1861; first lord of the treasury from July 6, 1846, till Feb. 26, 1852; secretary of state for foreign affairs from Dec. 28, 1852, till Feb. 20, 1853, when he retained a seat in the cabinet, but held no appointment; lord president of the council from June 12, 1854, till Feb. 7, 1855; appointed to be the unpaid charity Commissioner for England and Wales, July 8, 1854; sent on a special mission to Vienna, Feb. 11, 1855; appointed one of a committee of council to superintend the application of any sums of money voted by parliament for the purpose of promoting public education, Feb. 28, 1855; secretary of state for the colonies from March to July, 1855; appointed secretary of state for foreign affairs, June 19, 1859; and one of the committee of council to superintend the application of any sums of money voted by parliament for the purpose of promoting public education, July 6, 1859; was in attendance upon Her Majesty when she proceeded to Coburg in Sept. and Oct. 1860; prime minister, Nov. 1865, to July, 1866.

RUSSELL, JAMES.—Graduated B.A. at Queen's University, Ireland, 1863; M.A., 1873; LL.B., obtaining university gold medal, 1874; called to the bar at Lincoln's-inn, Easter term, 1874; appointed to Hong Kong cadetship, August, 1865; government interpreter, 1st December, 1867; private secretary, February, 1868; police magistrate, 1870.

RUSSELL, THE VEN. ARCHDEACON, P. T.—Vicar-general of the Roman Catholic Church, South Australia.

RUTHERFORD, G.—Collector of customs, Natal, 1853.

RUTHERFORD, W.—Employed on the un-fixed establishment of the surveyor-general's department, Ceylon, from 15th March, 1859; assistant surveyor, January, 1871.

ST. HELENA, 2nd Bishop of (founded 1859)—RIGHT REV. THOMAS EARLE WELBY, D.D.—Appointed rector of Newton, Lincolnshire, in 1847, but resigned that living on becoming a colonial chaplain at the Cape; was archdeacon of George Town, from 1856 till May, 1862, when he was consecrated bishop of St. Helena. This colony was part of the see of Cape Town previously to the 6th June, 1859, when it was constituted a diocese, together, with the islands of Ascension and Tristan d'Acunha; the population is about 7,000.

ST. HILL, RICHARD AUGUSTUS.—Native of island of St. Vincent; assistant judge of supreme court of judicature in that island; appointed, 1866 first appointment in colonial service as coroner, 1842; resigned that office in 1851; has been a justice of the peace for the island 34 years; one of a bench of magistrates selected to carry out the duties of police magistrate for the Kingston district, during the abeyance of the Act in 1850; acted as magistrate (police) for the Grenadines district in 1859; for several years an assessor and appraiser of taxable objects, &c.

ST. PERN, J. G.—Clerk to the stipendiary magistrate, Savanne, Mauritius, Sept. 1853; appointed district clerk, 1860.

SALMON, C. S.—Appointed sub-collector of customs and J. P., British Sherbro, 23rd April, 1866; acted as manager and coroner of British Sherbro from 23rd April, 1866, to 8th Feb. 1867, and from 18th Dec. 1867, to 6th March, 1868; land commissioner for Sherbro, 4th April, 1867; acted as collector of customs, Sierra Leone, from May to Oct., 1868; also as registrar for shipping; collector of customs, Gold Coast, 28th Dec., 1869; acted as chief magistrate and judicial assessor, Gold Coast, from 8th April to 2nd Nov. 1870; chief civil commissioner, Seychelles (Mauritius), 1874.

SAMUEL, SAUL, C.M.G. (1874).—Late post-master-general of New South Wales; vice-president of the executive council and representative of the government in the legislative council of that colony; has also held office in four previous administrations as minister for finance and trade; was first elected in October, 1854, to represent the united counties of Roxburgh and Wellington in the old legislative council, before the introduction of responsible government in the colony; he afterwards represented various constituencies in the legislative assembly, his last election being for the metropolitan electorate of East Sydney, and continued in that branch of the legislature until May, 1872, when he resigned to accept a seat in the legislative council to represent the government in that house. Mr. Samuel, during his parliamentary career has been the author of several measures
which have become law — amongst others, the Navigation Act. In 1873, Mr. Samuel was appointed special commissioner by the government of the colony to visit New Zealand, England, and America, to make arrangements for the establishment of a mail service between the United Kingdom and the Australasian colonies by way of the United States; he resigned, 1875, with the rest of the Parkes ministry.

SANDERS, EDWARD HOWARD.—Formerly a 1st lieutenant in the Imperial Austrian 6th Dragoons, in which regiment he served for six years, leaving them in 1855 for the purpose of accepting a commission in Her Majesty's service, with the view of serving his own country in the field during the Crimean war; he was appointed lieutenant and adjutant of the 2nd Hussars, British German Legion, commanded by Lord Elphinstone, and served in them until they were disbanded; appointed stipendiary magistrate and gold commissioner of British Columbia, in April, 1859; also member of the legislative council.

SANDESON, FREDERICK JAMES.—Appointed clerk in treasury, South Australia, 26th June, 1854; secretary to Lands Titles Commissioners, 1st Dec., 1862; and secretary to attorney-general, 1st Dec., 1870.

SANDFORD, SIR FRANCIS RICHARD, KNT. BACHEL (creat. 1863) C.B.—Educated at Glasgow University and Balliol College, Oxford; was 1st class in classics, 1846, and graduated M.A. Oxon and LL.D. Glasgow; entered civil service as examiner privy council office, 1848, assistant secretary, 1854; knighted by patent for his services as secretary to the commissioners for the exhibition of 1862; assistant under-secretary of state for the colonies, December, 1868, to 30th January, 1870; secretary to committee of council on education, 1870.

SANDFORD, THE RIGHT REV. CHARLES WALDEGRAVE, D.D.—A bishop exercising episcopal functions over the same region as the former bishop of Gibraltar; appointed 1874.

SANGSTER, C. F. A.—Appointed clerk and accountant to the police department, Hong Kong, 1860; 2nd clerk in registrar-general's office, 1864; clerk of the supreme court, April, 1874; also deputy sheriff.

SANGUINETTI, FREDERICK S.—Is a second-class clerk in the office of the colonial secretary, Jamaica. Has acted on three occasions as a 1st class clerk.

SARGEAUNT, W. C., C.M.G. (1875).—Appointed clerk in the office of the secretary of state for the colonies, Feb., 1848; was permitted whilst on the establishment of that office to hold the appointment of colonial secretary of Natal from 1853 to 1858; was a member of the executive and legislative councils of that colony, a justice of the peace for the same, and lieut.-colonel of the Natal carbiniers, a corps of cavalry yeomanry; returned to the colonial office in 1858, and was appointed acting lieut.-governor of St. Vincent in 1859; returned to the colonial office, and was promoted an assistant clerk, 1860; appointed crown agent for the colonies, 1862.

SARGENT, SIR CHARLES, KNT. BACH. (1861).—Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge, 1843; 5th wrangler; called to the bar, Lincoln's-inn, 1848; formerly chief justice of the Ionian Islands; now one of the puisne judges, Bombay.

SARTORIUS, MAJOR REGINALD WILLIAM, C.M.G., V.C. (1874).—6th regiment of Bengal Cavalry, appointed to the Order of St. Michael and St. George for service in the Ashantee war, 1873-4, under Sir J. H. Glover, and received the Victoria Cross for an act of conspicuous gallantry in saving a wounded sergeant-major of Houssas.

SCHOLTZ, ROBERT IRWIN.—Was appointed clerk to the civil commissioner and resident magistrate of King William's Town, Cape Colony, 10th April, 1868, also distributor of stamps; appointed clerk in the deeds office at Klip Drift, Griqualand West, 5th August, 1872; chief clerk to the resident magistrate of Du Toits Pau, Griqualand West, 15th September, 1872; chief clerk to the attorney-general of Griqualand West, and clerk of the peace for the province, 10th July, 1873.

SCHÜRER, GEO. H.—Appointed clerk in the Treasury of British Honduras, July, 1869; keeper of the public cemeteries, September, 1871; private secretary to lieutenant-governor Cairns, July, 1872; performed duty as clerk to the colonial secretary of that colony for a short time, in conjunction with duties in the colonial treasury; justice of the peace, September, 1874; assistant collector of customs of the Gold Coast, November, 1874, to May, 1875; sent on special mission to Quittah, May, 1875, and received thanks of Governor-in-Chief for services in connection with the district accounts; assistant-collector and acting treasurer of Lagos, June, 1875, to January, 1876, also ex officio registrar of shipping and shipping master; commissary of taxation, British Guiana, Feb., 1876.

SCOTT, CHAS. W.—Employed as an extra clerk in the colonial office from 1840; appointed clerk in the registry department in 1852; clerk in the general department, July, 1870.

SCOTT, SIR JOHN, K.C.M.G. (1874).—Was employed in the foreign office on the affairs of the North American boundary commission, from 1840 to 1843; was appointed, in 1843, secretary to the boundary commission, established in conformity with the Ashburton Treaty of 1842, to define and mark out on the spot the boundary agreed upon in that treaty, in which operations he voluntarily undertook an active share in the explorations, surveys, and other field duties of the commission, and for which he received the special approbation of the secretary of state; at the termination of this com-
mission, in 1848, was appointed surveyor-general to the new settlement of Labuan; became acting lieutenant-governor and treasurer in 1849, and was appointed lieut.-governor of the colony by commission dated Nov. 1850; in March, 1856, was transferred from the government of Labuan to that of Natal, which government he held to the end of Dec. 1865; appointed governor of British Guiana.

SCOTT, RICHARD WILLIAM, Q.C.—Born, 1825; called to the bar of Upper Canada, 1848; created a Q.C., 1867; sat in the legislative assembly of Canada from 1867 to 1873, and while there carried the separate school act of Upper Canada; returned to the Ontario Assembly at Confederation, 1867; retired on his entrance into the Dominion Government, November, 1878; called to the senate, 13th March, 1874; was speaker of the Ontario assembly from 7th to 21st December, 1871; a member of executive council and commissioner of crown lands for same province, from latter date until 7th November, 1873, when sworn of the Queen's privy council; appointed secretary of state of Canada, 9 January, 1874; is ex officio registrar-general of Canada, and has civil control of the mounted police force, enrolled for service in the north-west territories of the Dominion.

SCOTT, W. H.—Local superintendent, Mauritius railways, 20th Jan., 1864; general manager of railways, May, 1870.

SEALY, SIR JOHN, K.C.M.G. (1874), (C.M.G. 1869).—Educated at Exeter College, Oxford, where he was 2nd class in classics, 1829; graduated M.A., 1833; called to the bar at the Middle Temple, in Nov. 1833; was solicitor-general of Barbados from 1841 to 1846, when he was appointed attorney-general of that colony. Is also chancellor of the diocese; was for many years a member of the house of assembly; resigned his seat, and was appointed a member of council in 1858. Retired on a pension, 1874. Resigned seat in council, 1876.

SEALY, THOMAS.—Entered the army, May, 1841; accompanied the 10th hussars to India, 1846; from thence, via Egypt, to the Crimea; present at the fall of Sebastopol (medal and clasp and Turkish medal); entered civil service convict department, April, 1857; appointed superintendent of prisons, Trinidad, 23rd May, 1870; selected to fill the post of superintendent of the penal settlement, Massaruni, British Guiana, 26th October, 1873.

SEMPER, HUGH R.—Member of legislature, St. Kitts, 1857; member of executive council, Montserrat, 1860; called to the bar (Middle Temple), 1866; crown law officer, Tortola, 1868; attorney-general, St. Kitts, 1870; attorney-general, Leeward Islands, 1872; attorney-general, Barbados, 1874.

SEMPER, JOHN RAWLINS.—Queen's counsel, Montserrat, appointed 1844. Is a member of the executive council, solicitor-general, Antigua; chief justice of St. Kitts, Nevis, and Anguilla, 1867; and judge of the court of appeal; 1st puisne judge, Leeward Islands, 1873.

SEMPER, R.E., M.R.C.S.—Medical officer, district 6; acting president of legislative assembly St. Kitts, and member of executive council.

SHAND, SIR CHAS. FARQUHAR, KNT. (creat. 1869).—Advocate, LL.D., Edinburgh, took academical honours every year, and repeatedly the first; author of "The Practice of the Court of Session," &c.; was an advocate depute, and counsel for the lords of the treasury, and the hon. commissioners of woods and forests in Scotland; chairman of the united industrial or ragged schools; director of the philosophical institution; and captain in the volunteer rifles, Edinburgh; appointed chief-justice of Mauritius in May, 1860; is also judge of the vice-admiralty Court.

SHARPE, HENRY.—Provost-marshal, Grenada; appointed 1855; with which office was combined, November, 1874, that of inspector of police.

SHARPE, W. E. T.—Educated at Trinity College, Dublin, where he obtained a scholarship, and graduated B.A. 1857; appointed a writer to the government of Ceylon, 1857; assistant government agent, Kurunegalla, 1860; and assistant agent, Kandy, 1861; promoted to district judgeship of Batticaloa, Aug. 1865; assistant Government agent, Badulla, 1868; acting government agent, north-western province, June, 1873.

SHAW, EDWARD WINGFIELD.—Retired captain royal navy, when lieutenant of H.M.S. "Plumper;" on the west coast of Africa, in 1858 and 1854, during an attack of Ashantees served on shore with Gold Coast corps as gunnery officer, and instructed that regiment in field and battery drill (their own adjutant and instructor having been killed by an explosion); for this he received the thanks of the secretary of state for the colonies; appointed private secretary to governor-in-chief of Leeward Islands in 1863; administered the government of Montserrat from April, 1865, to March, 1866; lieutenant-governor, Malacca, December, 1868.

SHAW, GILBERT.—Admitted to practice as an attorney-at-law in the supreme court of Jamaica in February, 1829; appointed clerk to the magistrates of Clarendon, 1st January, 1839; custos rotulorum of Vere, March, 1847; clerk of the peace, and magistrates' clerk of Vere, November, 1848; elected member of the house of assembly for Clarendon in December, 1859; appointed clerk of the vestry for Vere, March, 1862; served as a commissioner to inquire into and report upon the working of the immigration laws in May, 1867; appointed clerk of the Spanish Town district court, November, 1867, and provost-marshal general of the island, 1st June, 1871 (now abolished); appointed a stipendiary magistrate for St. Catherine's, July, 1874; acted as judge of the Spanish Town district court.

SHAW, GILBERT LAING.—Supernumerary clerk in the colonial secretary's office, Jamaica, April, 1866; third class clerk, 1st Sept., 1867; clerk of petty sessions for the parish of St. Catherine, 1st June, 1870.

SHAW, HENRY.—Appointed treasurer of St. Vincent, Feb. 1864; acting clerk of courts and keeper of records, 1850 (Honduras) Queen's advocate, full commission, May 30, 1851; coroner, Feb. 1857; nominee of the crown in the legislative assembly, 1861; was acting treasurer of St. Vincent from July, 1863, until his confirmation in that appointment in 1864.

SHAW, JOHN.—Late lieut. Longford militia; appointed chief clerk, customs department, 1863; acting collector, 1864, and collector and controller of customs, Sierra Leone, 1865, which office he at present holds; appointed also a commissioner for settling claims to lands, 1864; while on leave in England, during the Ashanti war, placed his services at the disposal of the secretary of state, and was by him directed to proceed to Lagos and assume the duties of collector of customs and colonial secretary in room of Captain Lees, transferred to the Gold Coast; administered the Government of Lagos from July to September, 1874; appointed treasurer of Sierra Leone, 1875.

SHEPPARD, WILLIAM TYNDALL.—Educated at Harrow and Trinity College, Cambridge (graduate, 1855); appointed clerk, railway department, South Australia, in April, 1856; clerk of court of insolvency, August, 1858; secretary to attorney-general, February, 1866; secretary to commissioner of public works, July, 1869; secretary to commissioner of crown lands and immigration, August, 1874; under treasurer, May, 1875.

SHEPSTONE, JOHN.—Assistant magistrate, P. Maritzburg, Natal, 1865.

SHEPSTONE, SIR THEOPHILUS, K.C.M.G. (1876), (C.M.G., 1869).—Appointed, Jan. 8, 1835, head-quarter interpreter of the Kafr language at the Cape, and served on the staff of Sir Benjamin D'Urban, governor and commander-in-chief, during the Kafr war of 1835; appointed clerk to the agent-general for native tribes on the frontiers of the Cape Colony, 1836; sent to accompany the first military expedition from the Cape to Natal, 1838; created justice of the peace under the Act, 6 & 7 Will. IV., to 25th degree south latitude; returned to the Cape Colony in 1839; appointed resident diplomatic agent to the Hlambe tribes, and superintendent of Fingoes at Fort Peddie, on the frontiers of Cape Colony, 1839; appointed diplomatic agent to and over the tribes inhabiting the colony of Natal, 1845; captain-in-chief of the native force in Natal, 1848; appointed to control, revise, and direct the administration of justice among the natives in that colony, according to native law, 1849; proposed and personally carried out a scheme for the taxation of the native population in the colony, which yielded about 10,000l. the first year, and now amounts to upwards of 16,000l. per annum; appointed judicial assessor Natal, under ordinance No. 1, 1855; was captain of the native police corps, from its appointment in 1848 to 1854, when it was disbanded; and has been engaged on various special missions and services in the colony not here enumerated; appointed secretary for native affairs, 1856; and member of the executive and legislative councils in that colony in the same year; proceeded on a special mission in 1878 to crown the king of Zululand; repaired to England August, 1874, to confer with the secretary of state on the native policy of the Natal government; returned in December, 1874; revisited England, July, 1876, as delegate from Natal to the London South African conference; appointed special commissioner in connection with the territories adjoining the colony, 5th Oct., 1876.

SHERIFF, ROBERT FFRENCH.—Called to the bar, Inner Temple, in November, 1862; admitted to practice at the Antigua bar in 1863; appointed crown member of the legislative council there, 1867, and one of her Majesty's counsel, 1869; administered the government of Montserrat from May, 1869, to July, 1870; elected a representative of the presidency of Antigua in general council, Leeward Islands, May, 1872; acting chief justice, St. Christopher and Nevis, October, 1873; attorney-general, Leeward Islands, 1874.

SINGLETON, FRANCIS CORBET.—Clerk of the legislative council, government resident of the Murray district in Western Australia from 1840 to 1847; member of the legislative council of the colony of Western Australia, nominated by the crown from 1844 to 1847; auditor general of South Australia from May 8, 1847 to Jan. 1851; clerk of the executive council, South Australia, from Dec. 1850 to Dec. 1851; clerk of the legislative council, South Australia, as a nominated council, from Dec. 1850 to Aug. 1851; clerk of the legislative council, under partly elected council, from Aug. 1851 to Feb. 1857; clerk of legislative council under Constitution Act, from Feb. 1857.

SKINNER, ALLAN MACLEAN.—Called to the bar, June, 1867; appointed, after competitive examination, to the civil service of the Straits Settlements, Nov., 1868; appointed acting sheriff of Singapore, after qualifying in Malay, Jan., 1871; confirmed in that appointment, April, 1871; appointed acting magistrate of province Wellesley, Penang, April, 1871; accompanied, July, 1871, the expedition to Salangore; appointed, in January, 1873, inspector of schools, to report on the state of education; he is also inspector of prisons, hospitals, and asylums for the colony; attended the governor in the Island of Pangkor, during the negotiations with the headmen of Perak, in January, 1874; in August gazetted acting assistant colonial secretary and clerk of the councils; appointed in Feb., 1876, acting postmaster-general.

SKINNER, T., C.M.G. (Creat. 1869).—Was formerly a major in the army, joined his regiment in Ceylon in 1819; was selected by Sir Edward Barnes to open a section of the road between Colombo and Kandy, 1820; employed from this time till 1837 on the staff in laying out lines of communication throughout the colony, and in carrying out a trigonometrical survey and sketch of the mountain zone, comprising the Upper Kan-
dian provinces, and subsequently the greater portions of the island. The result of these surveys is published in two maps, by the late General John Fraser, deputy quarter-master-general of Ceylon; appointed to the charge of the combined departments of surveyor-general and civil engineer, Ceylon, 1838; commissioner of roads, 1841; to which, in 1859, the civil engineer department was added; acting auditor-general, 1859, and again 1865. Retired July, 1867.

SKINNER, T. E. B.—Appointed a writer to the government of Ceylon, Oct. 1860; acting assistant agent, Kurunégalla, March, 1862, in which appointment he was confirmed in the following May; assistant agent at Nuwara Eliya, 1863; acting district judge, Batticaloa, January, 1866; fiscal central province, 1867; postmaster-general, 1872.

SLADE, J. G.—Appointed colonial secretary, Labuan, September, 1867; resident magistrate, Fremantle, W. Australia, Sept. 1868.

SLADEN, SIR CHARLES, K.C.M.G. (1875), (C.M.G. 1870).—Was a very early settler in the colony of Victoria; for many years practised as a solicitor; held the office of treasurer in the government of Mr. Haines, and was chief secretary from May to July, 1868; is a doctor of laws of the Melbourne University.

SMALE, SIR JOHN, KNIGHT BACH. (1874).—Called to the bar, Inner Temple, April, 1842; chief justice, Hong Kong, 1866; attorney-general 1860.

SMART, J. E.—Educated at Tiverton; appointed a writer in the Ceylon civil service, Sept. 1869; acting police magistrate, Panvila, June, 1872; acting police magistrate, Kalpitiya, June, 1873.

SMEETON, S. P.—Appointed extra clerk in the office of the secretary of state for the colonies, June, 1862; first class clerk in the colonial secretary's office, Jamaica, June, 1870.

SMITH, ALBERT JAMES, Q.C.—Born, 1822; called to the bar of New Brunswick, 1847; is a Q.C.; sat in New Brunswick assembly from 1852 until 1867, when returned to house of commons, where he remains; was a member of the executive council, New Brunswick, from 1856 to 1863, and also for a short period in 1866; attorney-general from 1862 to 1863, when he retired from the Government; held same office in his own administration, 1865; was a delegate to England with the present Judge Fisher, 1858, on the subject of the intercolonial railway; to the same country, with the present Chief Justice Allan, on public business, 1865; and to Washington, with Hon. Messrs. Galt (now Sir A. T.), Howland and Henry, on the subject of reciprocal trade, Jan., 1866; declined the chief justiceship of New Brunswick, 1866; the lieut.-governorship of the same province, 1873; and the ministership of justice of the Dominion, June, 1874; sworn of the privy council, and appointed minister of marine and fisheries, 7th Nov., 1873.

SMITH, CECIL CLEMENTI.—Educated at St. Paul's School and at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge; graduated as B.A., 1862, M.A., 1868; elected student interpreter, Hong Kong, March, 1862; appointed registrar general 13th March, 1865; acting police magistrate, June, 1865; acting colonial secretary, 1867; appointed member of executive council, 1869; acting colonial secretary, February, 1872, to December, 1873; appointed treasurer, 1871; acted as colonial secretary in Oct. 1874, and also from 11th March, 1875.

SMITH, DANIEL T.—Receiver-general and treasurer of Turks Islands, 1851; was a member of the executive council and comptroller of customs; now chief commissioner of Turks Islands.

SMITH, E. A. M.—Manager of British Combo, Gambia, 4 June, 1866; manager of McCarthy's Island, 1876.

SMITH, E. T.—Educated at Tonbridge School, and Brasenose College, Oxford, where he graduated B.A., 1858; called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn, Jan 1862; member of the Home Circuit, and practised at the East and West Kent sessions; was appointed stipendiary magistrate, Falkland Islands, August, 1878; notary public, June, 1874; stipendiary justice, British Guiana, 1876.

SMITH, SIR FRANCIS, KNT. (created, 1862).—Graduated B.A. at London University 1840; called to the bar at the Middle Temple in May, 1842; appointed solicitor-general for the colony of Tasmania, 1849; attorney-general, 1854; was a member of the legislative assembly, 1849-60, and of the executive council, 1855-60; raised to the bench as a puisne judge of the supreme court, 1860; appointed chief justice, May, 1870.

SMITH, FREDERICK BONHAM.—Entered the colonial secretary's office, Barbados, in Jan., 1859; was in the office of the governor-in-chief of the Windward Islands from 1860 to 1866; appointed police magistrate of Christ Church, Barbados, in Oct., 1866; appointed senior police magistrate of Bridgetown and St. Michael in Sept., 1873.

SMITH, HENRY EDWIN.—Temporary clerk in colonial secretary's office, Tasmania, 1848; promoted to the survey department in 1849 served 22 years in that department; first class clerk, 1859; first lieutenant and adjutant, Buckingham rifles, 1860; transferred to colonial secretary's office, 1871, and appointed chief clerk in that office, 1873.

SMITH, KNT. BACHEL. (Created 1870); C.M.G. (1869).—Sir John Lucie Smith.—Called to the bar, Middle Temple, Nov. 1849; was solicitor-general of British Guiana from 1852 to 1855; appointed attorney-general, 1855; and acting chief justice, 1863; chief justice of Jamaica, 1869.

SMITH, PHILIP AUSTIN.—Chief justice, Bahamas, July, 1876.

SMITH, ROBERT, L.F.P. & S.—Graduated at Glasgow, 1865; appointed deputy inspector of health of shipping, Dec. 1865; assistant colonial surgeon, April, 1866; deputy coroner for Freetown and eastern districts.

SMITH, WILLIAM FREDERICK HAYNES.—Called to the bar, Middle Temple, 6 June, 1863; appointed solicitor-general, British Guiana, Oct. 1865; promoted to be attorney-general of that colony, Oct. 1874.

SMITHER, J. G.—Appointed architect assistant in public works department, Ceylon, 1866.

SMYTH, ARTHUR.—Resident magistrate, Wynberg division, Cape Colony, appointed March, 1863; was clerk there from 1849 to 1863; C.C. and R.M. Humansdorp.

SMYTH, MAJOR-GEN. EDWARD SELBY.—Served as brigade-major to the forces in the Southern Concan and Sawant Wanee country during the campaign of 1844-45, and was present at the attack and capture of several strong stockades, as well as in the operations before the mountain forts of Monohur, and at their final assault; also at the forcing of the Kirwattee Pass, and subsequent occupation of the country below the Ghats; served also in the Kaffir war of 1851-52 (medal), and mentioned in general orders for coolness and intre-
pidity in command of a column in action in the Fish River Bush—brevet major; with the expedition north of the Orange River in 1852-53, afterwards as deputy-assistant quarter-master-general of the 2nd division; and subsequently as D.-Adj.-Gen. and D.-Q.-M.-Gen. to the forces in South Africa from January, 1854, to July, 1860; commanding the troops, Mauritius, from 13th April, 1870; assumed the administration of the government, 3rd June, 1870; and from 19 August till 29 September, 1871, was acting secretary to the government in the eastern provinces, Cape of Good Hope, in 1859, whilst employed there as Quarter-master-general of the army, and was in spectator-general of Irish militia from 1861 till October, 1867; appointed a special magistrate for the county and city of Dublin in 1867; appointed to command the Canadian militia, 1874.

SMYTH, J. A. R.—Educated at Marlborough, and Trinity College, Dublin; writer, Ceylon civil service, 1868; acting police magistrate, Charakachcheri, May, 1870; ditto at Avissawela, Sept. 1870; police magistrate, Panadura, 1871; acting assistant government agent, Galle, June, 1872; ditto, ditto, Jaffna, Nov. 1872; ditto, ditto, Mullaitivu, March, 1873; landing and tide surveyor, Galle, Sept. 1873; to continue to act at Mullaitivu.

SMYTHE, WILLIAM H.—Chief clerk in customs department, St. Helena.

SNAGG, RICHARD, M.R.C.S.E., L.R.C.P., Edin., and L.M.—Medical officer, No. 3 district, St. Vincent, late assistant-surgeon, Great Western Railway, Swindon, Wiltshire.

SNAGG, SIR WM. KNT. BACH. (Creat. 1859.)—Called to the bar at the Middle Temple, 1829; was appointed solicitor-general of Grenada, May, 1835; attorney-general, July, 1847; and chief justice of Antigua and Montserrat, 1856; chief justice of British Guiana, 1868.

SNOWDEN, FRANCIS.—Educated at Rugby and University College, Oxford; graduated M.A. in 1854; in the same year was called to the English bar; practised on the western circuit and at the Bristol, Bath, and Salisbury borough sessions; in 1862 was appointed counsel for the treasury at the Salisbury sessions; in 1868 made a supernumerary revising barrister; acted as deputy county court judge; appointed senior magistrate, Straits Settlements, Nov. 1871; senior puisne judge, 1873; puisne judge, supreme court, Hong Kong, March, 1874.

SOLOMON, GEORGE.—Member of the legislative council, Jamaica, 1873.

SOMERSET, FITZROY MOLYNEUX HENRY, son of the late Right Honourable Lord William G. H. Somerset.—Is an officer of royal engineers, and a colonel in the army of 25th January, 1871; was appointed a member of the legislative and privy councils of Bermuda, 1874; and was acting governor and commander-in-chief of that colony from May to November, 1874; has also served in Canada and the Mediterranean.

SOUTHHEY, R., C.M.G. (1872).—Colonial secretary, Cape of Good Hope, 22nd July, 1864; was captain of corps of guides during the Kaffir war of 1834-1846; resident agent and magistrate to the Kaffir tribes of Umkai, Novebi, and Seyolo, at fort Murray, province of Queen Adelaide, 1836; secretary to high commissioner, Dec. 1847 to 1850. During this period was present at the battle of Boomplaats, and subsequently acted as president of war tribute commission in the Orange River Sovereignty; civil commissioner and resident magistrate of Swellendam, Feb. 1850, to May, 1852; acting secretary to government, Cape Town, May, 1852, to May, 1854; civil commissioner and resident magistrate at Swellendam, May, 1854, to Feb. 1855; secretary to lieut.-governor of Graham's Town, March, 1855, to Jan. 1859; auditor-general, Jan. 1859, to April, 1859; secretary to lieut.-governor, Graham's Town, April, 1859, to Aug. 1860; acting colonial secretary, Cape Town, Aug. 1860, to Jan. 1862; treasurer-general, Jan. 1862, to July, 1864; lieut.-govr. of Griqualand, Dec., 1872, till 1875.

SPENCER, H. H.—Appointed 1st officer to the colonial steamer "Dover," May, 1860; commander, 1863; served in the Baddiboo, Quiah, and Tubabcolong wars; transferred to Sierra Leone, Nov., 1866, as harbour-master and superintendent of lighthouse.

SPENCER, J. A.—Police-inspector, Mauritius, 1 Jan., 1857; superintendent of police, 7 Sept., 1859.

SPERLING, R. A.—Appointed assistant civil engineer and commissioner of roads, Ceylon, 1857; acting provincial assistant, north-western province, 1866.

SPEEDY, T. C. S.—Served in Her Majesty's 81st regiment from 1854 to 1860. During the Indian mutiny of 1857-1858 was present at the taking of Mungultana, near Sitana, during the Eusufzai expedition under Sir Sidney Cotton, K.C.B. (medal); served as adjutant of the 10th regiment Punjab infantry at Dera Ismail Khan, north-west frontier of India; was British vice-consul at Massowah, Abyssinia, in 1864; served in the New Zealand militia from 1864 to 1867; was captain and adjutant of the Waikate militia; served in the Abyssinian expeditionary force, 1867-68, on Sir Robert Napier's staff—intelligence department; present at the action of Arogie and capture of Magdala (medal); appointed by Her Majesty guardian to Prince Alamaya Simyen, son of the late King Theodore, of Abyssinia; district superintendent of Oudh police till 15th March, 1871; appointed commissioner of police, Penang, 14th April, 1871; now assistant British resident at Laroot.

SPROAT, GILBERT MALCOLM.—Educated for the India civil service; went to Vancouver Island in 1860; founded the settlement of Alberni; was magistrate and collector of customs there; was joint secretary of the committee in London for improving the condition of merchant seamen; chairman of the association for watching the affairs of British Columbia; was agent-general for British Columbia, 1872 to 1876; appointed, Sept., 1876, joint commissioner by the governments of Canada and British Columbia for the settlement of the Indian land controversy; is author of Scenes and Studies of Savage Life and other works; won the first prize of 200l. for the best essay on the British opium policy in India and China, Sir Bartle Frere, Sir C. Trevelyan, and Sir L. Mallet, being the judges.

SPROTT, ROBERT PORTER, M.D., Edinburgh.—Medical officer, No. 1 district, St. Vincent.

STAPLES, H. T.—Appointed assistant colonial surgeon, medical department, Ceylon, 1869.

STAWEll, KNT. BACHEL. (Creat. 1857.)—SIR WILLIAM FOSTER STAWEll.—Chief justice of Victoria.

ST. BERNARD, J. J.—Is a colonial revenue officer, Grenada; appointed assistant clerk, colonial secretary's office, 1867; colonial revenue officer, 1871; acting chief clerk, colonial secretary's office, 1872; acted as postmaster during 1876.

STEEL, T.—Appointed a writer in the Ceylon civil service, July, 1856; attached to government agent's office, Kurunegalla, Nov., 1856; acting as—
sistant government agent at Galle, 1857; acting assistant government agent at Galle, May, 1859; confirmed Dec., 1859; acting police magistrate at Kandy, Dec., 1863; confirmed in that office, May, 1865; acting assistant government agent, Hambantota, with judicial duties, July, 1869; confirmed in that appointment, Sept., 1869.

STEPHEN, KNT. BACHEL (Creet., 1846), C.B. (civil), 1862; K.C.M.G., 1874.—Sir ALFRED STEPHEN.—Was called to the bar at Lincoln's Inn, 1823; appointed solicitor-general of Van Diemen's Land in 1825; attorney-general of that colony in 1832; one of the judges of New South Wales in 1839; and chief justice there in 1854, on which occasion he received the honour of knighthood. Retired; appointed lieutenant-governor New South Wales, November, 1875.

STEPHEN, ALFRED H., M.A., of Trinity College, Cambridge.—Was ordained in 1849; appointed to the cure of St. Paul's, Sydney in 1855; canon in St. Andrew's cathedral in that city, 1870; is the son of Sir Alfred Stephen, C.B., chief justice of New South Wales.

STEVENS, T. H.—Appointed second clerk in treasury, Antigua, 1873; clerk in treasury, St. Kitts, 1874.

STEPHENSON, F. L.—Appointed junior clerk in the treasury, Jamaica, 1st June, 1852; promoted in the same department, 1861; appointed landings-waiter of H. M. customs, Falmouth, March, 1865, and locker and gauger at the same port, 1866; transferred as clerk and warehouse keeper to Montego Bay, Nov., 1867; appointed acting sub-collector of customs at that port, Aug., 1868; transferred to collector-general's office, Kingston, as customs statistical clerk, July, 1869; appointed acting chief clerk in the same office, 1870; and appointed to present office of chief clerk in H.M. customs at the port of Kingston, December, 1870.

STEWART, C. H.—Admitted an advocate of the supreme court of Ceylon, 1846; called to the English bar at Lincoln's Inn, 1863; was appointed deputy Queen's advocate, Jaffna, 1845, and deputy Queen's advocate, Kandy, in 1848; deputy Queen's advocate and one of the law officers of the crown for the island, 1852; acting district judge, Colombo, from January to June, 1860; acting 2nd puisne judge of the supreme court, 1864; appointed permanently one of the puisne justices, 1867.

STEWART, G.—Held the office of deputy Queen's advocate, western province, Ceylon, 1874; acting commissioner of requests, &c., Bentota, from 1854 to 1858; appointed commissioner of requests, &c., Harispattu, 1858; and acting commissioner of requests, &c., Gampola, 1861; in which appointment he was confirmed, 1862; acting district judge, Tangalla, 1864; acting commissioner of requests, Colombo, 1865; acting commissioner of requests, &c., Kandy, 1867; acting police magistrate, Colombo, Oct., 1871; acting police magistrate, Kandy, Dec., 1871; district judge, Ratnapura, Sept., 1872; continuing to act as police magistrate, Kandy.

STEWART, J.T.—Superintending office, public works department, Ceylon, 1865.

STILL, H. L.—Employed on the unfixed establishment of the surveyor-general's department, Ceylon, from Dec. 17, 1858, to July, 1870; assistant surveyor, July, 1870.

STODDART, J.—Appointed to the surveyor-general's department in Ceylon, 1866; assistant surveyor, Ceylon, 1868.

STODDART, W.—Employed on the unfixed establishment of the surveyor-general's department from January, 1867; assistant surveyor, January, 1871.

STONE, J. F.—Appointed superintendent of water police, Western Australia, 1866; was immigration agent, Perth, for several years previously.

STONE, R. SIDNEY, M.D., L.R.C.P., Lond., M.R.C.S.—Formerly house surgeon at St. Bartholomew's hospital, London; assistant surgeon and resident surgeon, civil hospital, Mauritius, Dec., 1864; government medical officer, vaccinator, and commissioner in lunacy for the district of Flacq, 1870; was chairman of the local board of health of Flacq until its abolition in 1874.

STRACHAN, W. H. P. F. M., Lieut.-Colonel.—Entered the army in 1852; lieutenant, 1853; captain, 1862; major, 1871; lieut.-colonel, 1874; on the staff as fort adjutant, at Bahamas, 1859 to 1861; inspector-general of police and a justice of the peace for the settlement of Bathurst, province of Gambia, 1867, where he also acted for some time as queen's advocate; commanded troops at Bahamas; British Honduras, member of executive and legislative councils, British Guiana and Gold Coast, member of both councils, and acting police magistrate of the latter colony in 1875.

STRACHEY, WILLIAM.—Appointed by Earl Grey in 1848 to be précis writer to the colonial office; retired 1870; was formerly in the Bengal civil service.

STRAHAN, Capt. Geo. C., R.A., C.M.G. (1875).—Entered the royal artillery, Oct. 1857; was appointed, Jan. 1859, aide-de-camp to the Right Hon. W. E. Gladstone, M.P., when lord high commissioner of the Ionian Islands; and Feb. 17th was appointed in the same capacity by the late Sir Henry Storks, G.C.M.G., K.C.B.; acted as chief secretary to the government of Malta during a portion of the year, 1868-9; colonial secretary, Bahamas, 1868; acting governor, Bahamas, from April, 1871, to May, 1873; appointed administrator of the government, Lagos, 1873; governor of the Gold Coast Colony, July, 1874; governor of the Windward Islands, 1876.

STRANGWAYS, HENRY BULL TEMPLER.—Visited South Australia in 1853-4; called to the bar at the Middle Temple, June, 1856; a member of the South Australian Parliament, Dec., 1857, to Feb., 1871; attorney-general, May, 1860, to May, 1861; commissioner of crown lands and immigration, May, 1861, to October, 1863, and again, March, 1865, to October, 1865; attorney-general and premier, October, 1868, to May, 1870; carried through the Parliament the first Act for the sale of land on credit, and arranged for the construction of the Central Australian telegraph line; appointed a magistrate for Somersetshire, 1871; permitted by the Queen to retain the title of Honourable in South Australia as a late member of the executive council.

STRAUBENZEE, G.C.B. (1875), (K.C.B. 1858).—GENERAL SIR CHARLES THOMAS VAN STRAUBENZEE.—Born at Malta, 17th Feb., 1812; entered the army, as ensign, 28th Aug., 1828; lieutenant, 22nd Feb., 1833; captain, 10th March, 1837; major, 27th Aug., 1843; brevet lieut.-colonel, 30th April, 1844; lieut.-colonel, 11th Nov., 1851; colonel, 20th June, 1854; major-general, 14th Aug., 1860; lieut.-general, 27th March, 1868; general, 29th April, 1875. Was present with his regiment, the 39th Foot, throughout the campaign in Coorg, 1834, and during the occupation and annexation of that territory. As major of the 39th, he succeeded to the command of the regiment during the action of Maharajpore, Gwalior, 29th Dec., 1843, for which battle he received his brevet lieut.-colonelcy, and remained in command during the disarmament
of the Gwalior forces. As brevet lieut.-colonel and major of the Buffs, he was appointed to the command of a field force in Ireland, encamped at Pilltown and Carrick-on-Suir, for the purpose of operating between Waterford and Clonmel, and consisting of a battery of artillery, two troops 4th light dragoons, seven companies of the Buffs, and two of the 85th light infantry, during the Smith O'Brien troubles in 1846. As lieut.-colonel, he commanded the British contingent in Greece during part of 1854 and 1855; and in April, 1855, proceeded to the Crimea, where he was appointed to command a brigade, and remained till July, 1856; was present at the two assaults on the Redan, in June and September; at the former he commanded a separate brigade, at the latter the 1st brigade light division, and was slightly wounded. On his return from the Crimea, he was appointed to the command of the 1st brigade, Dublin division, and remained there till ordered, in 1857, to China, to command a brigade, but before the commencement of operations he succeeded to the command of the forces; he commanded at the capture of Canton by assault, on 29th Dec., 1857, and was in command at all subsequent operations till relieved, in March, 1860. In 1861, Major-General Van Straubenzee proceeded to Bombay, and commanded the northern division, and, on Lieut.-General Sir Wm. Mansfield's appointment to command the Indian army, Sir Charles succeeded to that of Bombay, which he held nearly a year, till the arrival of Sir Robert Napier, in 1865; and returned to England early in 1866. Was appointed governor and commander-in-chief of Malta, in 1872. For the battle of Maharajpore, he received a brevet lieut.-colonelcy and the bronze star of Gwalior; for the Crimea, medal with clasp, companionship of the Bath, officer of the Legion of Honour, Sardinian and Turkish medals, and 3rd class of the Medjide; for China, K.C.B., medal and clasp. He was appointed colonel of the 47th Foot in 1865, and was removed to the colonelcy of the 39th Foot in 1867, and in 1875 was appointed a grand cross of the Bath.

STRETTEN, WILLIAM WARREN.—Educated at Tunbridge School; called to the bar, Lincoln's-inn, 6th June, 1857; appointed Queen's advocate, West Africa Settlements, Oct., 1874.

STUART, JOHN.—Clerk of the house of assembly, Newfoundland, 1855. Also secretary to the board of works, 1858.

STUART, MELVIN VICTOR DEBMONT.—Appointed temporary clerk in treasury department, Nassau, Bahamas, May, 1864; junior clerk, July, 1865; acting collector of revenue, Harbour Island, 1866, and Eleuthera, 1867; acting collector at Nassau, from July, 1870, to Jan., 1874; also from Dec., 1874, to Feb., 1875; 2nd clerk, or bookkeeper, March, 1875; measuring surveyor of shipping from Nov., 1864, to Oct., 1875; examining officer at Gold Coast, 1875.

SULLIVAN, FRED.—Appointed to governor's secretary's office, Jamaica, Christmas, 1852; employed therein as clerk from Feb., 1853; in 1859, being then chief clerk, acted as private secretary to Governor Darling, from May to Nov.; in May, 1860, confirmed in that appointment; held that office until March, 1861, when he was transferred to present office of chief clerk in the post office department; has acted on several occasions as postmaster for Jamaica; appointed postmaster for Jamaica, 1870.

SUTTON, CHARLES.—Entered the army, 1846; rose to be a lieutenant without purchase in Dec., 1853; acting barrack-master from 1st Sept., 1860, to 23rd June, 1862, when he retired; present at the assaults on Sebastopol, on the 18th June and 8th Sept., 1855. Has a Crimean medal and clasp, and Turkish medal; inspector of prisons, Mauritius, 1862; inspector of police, Bahamas, June, 1864.

SWAINSON, J. CURRIE.—Appointed clerk to the inspector of prisons, Jamaica, Feb., 6, 1866; transferred to colonial secretary's office as clerk of the third class, July 15, 1867; promoted to be a 2nd class clerk, Oct., 1874.

SWETTENHAM, F. A.—Appointed to the civil service, Straits Settlements, 1870; is attached to lieutenant-governor's office, Penang; assistant collector of land revenue, 1 Sept., 1872.

SWETTENHAM, J. A.—Educated at Clare Coll., Cambridge, where he obtained a scholarship in May, 1867; writer, Ceylon civil service, 1868; acting police magistrate, Harrispattu, Feb. 1870; police magistrate, Kayts, Sept. 1870, continuing to act at Harrispattu; acting assistant government agent, Galle, Dec. 1871; acting landing and tide surveyor, Galle, June, 1872; assistant collector of customs, Jaffna, Oct. 1872, to continue to act at Galle; acting district judge, Matare, April, 1873.

SYDNEY (AUSTRALIA), 2ND BISHOP OF.—Founded 1847.—RIGHT REV. FREDERIC BARKER, D.D.—Educated at Grantham School and at Jesus College, Cambridge, where he graduated A.B. 1829, M.A. 1835, D.D. 1854; became incumbent of Upton, Cheshire, 1830; of St. Mary's, Edge Hill, Liverpool, 1835; and of Baslow, Derbyshire, 1854; consecrated 1854; is author of "A Commentary on Twenty-six Psalms," &c.; is metropolitan bishop in Australia. The diocese originally included the whole of Australia, and bore that name; but in 1847 it was restricted to the central portion of the colony, and called by its present title, while additional bishops were nominated for Newcastle, Adelaide, Melbourne, and Perth; by patent, 19th October, 1854. The bishop is a metropolitan bishop, whose suffragans are the bishops of the above dioceses.

SYMonds, G. H.—Employed on the unfixed establishment of the surveyor-general's department, Ceylon, from Nov., 1857; assistant-surveyor, Jan., 1871.

SYMons, J. P.—Was employed in various offices under the government of Natal from 1850 to 1855; appointed master of the supreme court, July, 1855, and auditor of that colony, Aug., 1863.

SYRETT, ROBERT H.—Entered the civil service as landing waiter in the customs department, Gambia; transferred to the colonial hospital, as dispenser, June, 1871; appointed confidential clerk in the administrator's office, Jan., 1872; acting clerk of the legislative council, May, 1872; and acting first writer, Oct., 1872.

TACHE, J. C.—Chairman of the board of inspectors of asylums and prisons, Canada; secretary of board of registration and statistics in 1861; deputy to the minister of agriculture, 11th Aug., 1864; appointed to same office under dominion government, July, 1867.

TALBOT, ARTHUR PHILIP.—Appointed to be a cadet in service of the Straits Settlements, on 13th April, 1874.

TASCHEREau, Jean Thomas.—Called to the bar of Lower Canada, 1836; created a Q.C., 1860; appointed an assistant judge of the superior court, Lower Canada, 3rd Sept., 1855; a puisne judge of same court, 11th Feb., 1865; a puisne judge of the
